sentences.zh: 孫長卿

translations.literal: Sun Zhangqing
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhangqing

sentences.zh: 孫長卿，字次公，揚州人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhangqing, styled Cigong, was a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhangqing, whose courtesy name was Cigong, came from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以外祖朱巽任為秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Through his maternal grandfather Zhu Xun's appointment, he served as a collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a collator in the Secretariat through the influence of his maternal grandfather, Zhu Xun.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，巽守雍，命隨所取浮圖像入見。

translations.literal: During the Tianxi era, when Xun was prefect of Yong, he ordered him to bring along a Buddhist image he had obtained to an audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi reign period, while Zhu Xun was prefect of Yong, he had Sun bring a Buddhist image he had acquired to present at court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗方權聽天下事，嘉其年少敏占對，欲留侍東宮，辭以母疾。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was still regent over all affairs under Heaven, praised his youth and quick wit in replies, and wished to keep him to attend the Eastern Palace, but he declined citing his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong was then regent of the realm. He admired the young man's quick wit in conversation and wished to keep him at the crown prince's side, but Sun begged off, pleading his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 詔遷官知楚州糧料院。

translations.literal: An edict transferred his rank and made him supervisor of the Chuzhou grain provisions office.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict promoted him and appointed him supervisor of the grain provisions office at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡倉積米五十萬，陳腐不可食，主吏皆懼法，毋敢輕去，長卿為酌新舊均渫之，吏罪得免。

translations.literal: The prefectural granary had five hundred thousand accumulated measures of rice, rotten and inedible; the chief clerks all feared the law and dared not lightly dispose of it. Zhangqing apportioned old and new to mix and drain it evenly, and the clerks' offenses were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural storehouse held five hundred thousand bushels of rice that had rotted beyond use. The warehouse clerks feared prosecution and dared not discard any of it. Zhangqing arranged to blend the spoiled grain with fresh stock and draw it off evenly, sparing the clerks from punishment.

sentences.zh: 通判河南府。

translations.literal: Vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秋，大雨，軍營壞，或言某眾將叛，洛中讙然，長卿馳諭之曰：「天雨敗屋廬，未能葺，汝輩豈有欲叛意，得無有乘此動吾軍者邪？

translations.literal: In autumn, heavy rain damaged the military camps. Some said a certain body of troops would rebel; Luoyang seethed with alarm. Zhangqing rode in haste to address them, saying: "Heaven's rain has ruined our buildings, which cannot yet be repaired. Would you truly harbor thoughts of rebellion? Could it be rather that someone is stirring up our army by taking advantage of this?"
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, torrential rains wrecked the army camps. Rumors spread that certain units were about to mutiny, and panic swept Luoyang. Zhangqing galloped to the scene and rallied the men: "The rains have ruined our barracks before we could repair them. Do you truly mean to rebel? Or is someone trying to use this crisis to stir unrest in the ranks?"

sentences.zh: 」推首惡一人誅之，留宿其所，眾遂定。

translations.literal: He seized and executed the ringleader, stayed overnight at their quarters, and the troops were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested and executed the principal instigator, spent the night among the troops, and the army calmed at once.

sentences.zh: 詔汰三陵奉先卒，汰者群譟府下，長卿矯制使還，而具言不可汰之故，朝廷為止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a reduction of the guardian troops at the Three Imperial Mausoleums. Those marked for discharge raised a stormy clamor before the prefecture. Zhangqing, invoking discretionary imperial authority, ordered them back and set forth the reasons the reduction could not proceed; the court thereupon stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for cutting the guard detachments at the Three Imperial Mausoleums, the men facing discharge raised a tumult at the prefectural gate. Zhangqing issued orders under emergency authority to send them back, laid out why the cutback would not work, and the court abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 知和州，民訴人殺弟，長卿察所言無理，問其資，曰：「上等也。

translations.literal: As prefect of He Prefecture, a man lodged complaint that another had killed his younger brother. Zhangqing saw that what he said was unreasonable and asked his household registration status. He said: "It is of the first grade."
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of He Prefecture, a man came forward claiming someone had murdered his younger brother. Zhangqing found the story implausible and asked the man's household rank. "First grade," the man replied.

sentences.zh: 」「家幾人？

translations.literal: "How many people are in your household?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many people live in your household?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「惟此弟爾。

translations.literal: He said: "Only this younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: "Only this younger brother," he said.

sentences.zh: 」 曰：「然則汝殺弟也。

translations.literal: He said: "Then it was you who killed your brother."
translations.idiomatic: "Then you must be the one who killed him," Zhangqing said.

sentences.zh: 」鞫之，服，郡人神明之。

translations.literal: When he interrogated him, the man confessed; the people of the prefecture regarded him as divinely perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Under questioning the man confessed, and the people of the commandery hailed Zhangqing's judgment as inspired.

sentences.zh: 提點益州路刑獄，歷開封鹽鐵判官、江東淮南河北轉運使、江浙荊淮發運使。

translations.literal: As regional inspector of legal affairs for the Yizhou Circuit, then successively Kaifeng Salt and Iron Commissariat judge, transport commissioner for Jiangdong, Huainan, and Hebei, and grain-shipment commissioner for Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jing, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as regional inspector of legal affairs in the Yizhou circuit, then as salt and iron commissariat judge at Kaifeng, transport commissioner for Jiangdong, Huainan, and Hebei, and grain-shipment commissioner for Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jing, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 歲漕米至八百萬，或疑其多，長卿曰：「吾非欲事羨贏，以備饑歲爾。

translations.literal: When annual grain transport reached eight million measures, some doubted the quantity was too large. Zhangqing said: "I do not mean to amass surpluses for display; it is to prepare for years of famine."
translations.idiomatic: When annual shipments of grain reached eight million bushels, some questioned whether the figure was inflated. Zhangqing replied, "I am not padding the accounts for profit. This is a reserve against years of famine."

sentences.zh: 」議者謂楚水多風波，請開盱眙河，自淮趣高郵，長卿言：「地阻山回繞，役大難就。

translations.literal: Critics argued that the Chu waterways had too many storms and waves and requested opening the Xuyi River to carry from the Huai toward Gaoyou. Zhangqing said: "The terrain is blocked by winding mountains; the labor is great and hard to complete."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the Chu water route was too prone to storms and petitioned to open the Xuyi River, running from the Huai directly toward Gaoyou. Zhangqing objected that the land was broken by winding mountain barriers and that the project would demand enormous labor with little hope of success.

sentences.zh: 」事下都水，調工數百萬，卒以不可成，罷之。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Directorate of Waterways; laborers to the tune of millions were deployed, and in the end it could not be completed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the Directorate of Waterways, which deployed labor on a scale of millions. In the end the work could not be finished and was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時又將弛茶禁而收其徵，召長卿議，長卿曰：「本祖宗榷茶，蓋將備二邊之糴，且不出都內錢，公私以為便。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a plan to relax the tea monopoly and collect only its levies; Zhangqing was summoned to consult. Zhangqing said: "Originally the ancestors monopolized tea in order to prepare grain purchases for the two frontiers, and without spending money from within the capital—government and private interests alike found it convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The court was also weighing a loosening of the tea monopoly, retaining only its tax levy. Zhangqing was called in to advise. "Our founders imposed the tea monopoly," he said, "precisely to fund grain purchases for the northern and western frontiers without drawing on the capital treasury—an arrangement both public and private interests found useful."

sentences.zh: 今之所行，不足助邊糴什一，國用耗矣。

translations.literal: What is now proposed would scarcely assist frontier grain purchases by one part in ten; state revenue is being exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: "What you propose now," he said, "would barely supply one tenth of frontier grain needs. The state coffers would be drained instead."

sentences.zh: 」乃條所不便十五事，不從。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed fifteen inconvenient points; the court did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a list of fifteen objections. The court did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 改陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Transport Commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of grand transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，知慶州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he became prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 州據險高，患無水，蓋嘗疏引澗谷汲城中，未幾復絕。

translations.literal: The prefecture stood on perilous high ground and suffered lack of water; they had once dredged and drawn from ravine streams into the city, but before long it failed again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou occupied high, defensible ground and chronically lacked water. An earlier effort had diverted mountain streams into the city, but before long the supply failed again.

sentences.zh: 長卿鑿百井，皆及泉。

translations.literal: Zhangqing dug a hundred wells, all reaching springs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqing sank a hundred wells, each striking water.

sentences.zh: 泥陽有羅川、馬嶺，上構危棧，下臨不測之淵，過者惴恐。

translations.literal: At Niyang were the Luo River and Maliu Mountain; above were perilous trestle ways, below overlooked unfathomable abysses; those who passed feared in dread.
translations.idiomatic: At Niyang, near the Luo River and Maliu Mountain, travelers crossed trestleways hung above dizzying depths, passing in terror.

sentences.zh: 長卿訪得唐故道，闢為通塗。

translations.literal: Zhangqing investigated and found an old Tang route and opened it as a thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqing located an old Tang-era road and reopened it as a safe thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 加集賢院學士、河東都轉運使，拜龍圖閣直學士、知定州。

translations.literal: He was promoted Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Grand Transport Commissioner for Hedong, and received the title Dragon Diagram Hall Direct Academician and appointment as prefect of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and grand transport commissioner for Hedong, then granted the title of direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，河北地大震，城郭倉庾皆隤，長卿盡力繕補。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, a great earthquake struck Hebei; city walls and granaries all collapsed; Zhangqing exerted full effort to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xining reign, a massive earthquake struck Hebei, toppling city walls and state granaries. Zhangqing threw all his energy into repairs.

sentences.zh: 神宗知其能，轉兵部侍郎，留再任。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong knew his ability, transferred him to Vice Minister of War, and kept him for another term.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong recognized his competence, promoted him to vice minister of war, and ordered him to serve another term.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 長卿無文學，而長於政事，為能臣。

translations.literal: Zhangqing had no literary learning, but was long on government affairs and was a capable minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqing possessed no particular literary fame, but he excelled at practical governance and ranked among the empire's capable officials.

sentences.zh: 性潔廉，不以一毫取諸人。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and incorrupt; he never took a hair's breadth from others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was scrupulously honest and never accepted even the smallest favor from anyone.

sentences.zh: 定州當得園利八十萬，悉歸之公。

translations.literal: Ding Prefecture was entitled to eighty thousand in garden profits; he returned all to the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou was due eighty thousand in proceeds from public gardens; he turned every coin over to the state.

sentences.zh: 既沒，詔中使護其喪歸葬。

translations.literal: After his death, an edict dispatched an imperial messenger to escort his coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, the throne ordered an imperial envoy to escort his coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 周沆，字子真，青州益都人。

translations.literal: Zhou Hang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Yidu, Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hang, whose courtesy name was Zizhen, came from Yidu in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，知渤海縣。

translations.literal: He placed as jinshi and served as magistrate of Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi degree, he became magistrate of Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，縣人請留，既報可，而以親老求監州稅。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, the county people requested he stay; after approval was granted, he sought instead to supervise prefectural tax office, citing aged parents.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, the people petitioned to retain him; once that was approved, he asked instead to oversee a prefectural tax office, pleading the need to care for his elderly parents.

sentences.zh: 通判鳳翔，初置轉運判官。

translations.literal: Vice-prefect of Fengxiang; among the first appointed transport vice-commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Fengxiang and was one of the first transport vice-commissioners appointed.

sentences.zh: 沆使江西，求葬親，改知沂州。

translations.literal: Hang served in Jiangxi, sought to bury his parents, and was changed to prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Jiangxi, Hang obtained leave to bury his parents and was transferred to the prefecture of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官。

translations.literal: He served as investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the investigating magistrate's bench at Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湖南蠻唐、盤二族寇暴，殺居民，官軍數不利，以沆為轉運使。

translations.literal: The southern Man of the Tang and Pan clans pillaged violently, killing residents; government troops repeatedly fared poorly; Hang was made transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan, the Tang and Pan barbarian clans had been marauding, killing civilians, and repeatedly defeating government troops. Hang was appointed transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沆言：「蠻驟勝方驕，未易鬥力，宜須秋冬進兵。

translations.literal: Hang said: "The Man, having won sudden victories, are now arrogant; it is not easy to contest strength. We should wait until autumn and winter to advance troops."
translations.idiomatic: Hang argued, "Fresh from their victories, the barbarians are arrogant. Direct confrontation will not serve. We should wait until autumn and winter before moving troops."

sentences.zh: 且其地險氣毒，人驍悍，善用鋋盾，北軍不能𥒰。

translations.literal: Moreover the terrain is dangerous and the air poisonous; the people are fierce and skilled at hooked shields; northern troops cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Their country is rugged and malarial, and their warriors are fierce, adept with hooked shields. Troops from the north cannot break them.

sentences.zh: 請選邕、宜、融三州卒三千人習知山川技藝者，徑搗其巢，布餘兵絡山足，出則獵取之。

translations.literal: He requested selecting three thousand men from Yong, Yi, and Rong prefectures who knew mountains and possessed skills, to strike their nests directly, while deploying remaining troops along the mountain foothills to hunt them when they came out.
translations.idiomatic: Select three thousand men from Yong, Yi, and Rong who know the mountains and local fighting techniques. Send them straight at the enemy strongholds while the rest spread along the foothills to cut off anyone who tries to flee.

sentences.zh: 俟其勢窮力屈，乃可順撫。

translations.literal: Wait until their power is exhausted and strength spent, then they can be smoothly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they are cornered and spent can we bring them peacefully to heel.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷用其策，二族皆降。

translations.literal: The court used his strategy; both clans all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his strategy, and both clans submitted.

sentences.zh: 加直史館、知潭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted Direct Historiography Office drafting historian and prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made drafting historian in the Direct Historiography Office and appointed prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 他道兵來戍者，率兩期乃代，多死瘴癘，沆請以期為斷，戍人便之。

translations.literal: Troops coming from other circuits to garrison generally served two terms before replacement; many died of miasma. Hang requested that one term be set as the limit; garrison soldiers found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers sent from other circuits to garrison the area usually had to serve two full rotations before relief, and many succumbed to the local miasma. Hang petitioned to limit service to a single rotation, greatly easing the burden on the troops.

sentences.zh: 徙河東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 民盜鑄鐵錢，法不能禁，沆高估錢價，鑄者以無利，自息。

translations.literal: The people illicitly cast iron coin; the law could not prohibit it. Hang greatly raised the price of coin; casters found no profit and ceased on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Illegal iron coin casting plagued the region, and the law could not stop it. Hang sharply raised the official price of coin until casting brought no profit, and the illegal minting died away on its own.

sentences.zh: 入為度支副使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as deputy commissioner of the Revenue Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as deputy commissioner of the Revenue Branch.

sentences.zh: 儂智高亂定，仁宗命安撫廣西，諭之曰：「嶺外地惡，非賊所至處，毋庸行。

translations.literal: After Nong Zhigao's rebellion was settled, Renzong ordered him to pacify Guangxi and instructed him: "Beyond the ranges the land is vile; where the bandits have not reached, need not go."
translations.idiomatic: After Nong Zhigao's rebellion was suppressed, Renzong named him to pacify Guangxi and told him, "The country beyond the passes is savage. There is no need to venture where the rebels never went."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「君命，仁也；

translations.literal: He replied: "A lord's command is humanity;"
translations.idiomatic: Hang replied, "A sovereign's commission is an act of grace in itself;

sentences.zh: 然遠民罹塗炭，當布宣天子德澤。

translations.literal: yet distant people suffer flood and fire; one ought to spread abroad the Son of Heaven's virtue and grace.
translations.idiomatic: but the far-off people are still reeling from war and ruin. I should carry the Son of Heaven's kindness to every corner."

sentences.zh: 」遂往，遍行郡邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went, traveling through every prefecture and county.
translations.idiomatic: He went anyway, visiting every prefecture and county in the region.

sentences.zh: 民避寇棄業，吏用常法，滿半歲則聽人革佃。

translations.literal: When people fleeing bandits abandoned their occupations, officials applied the usual rule; after half a year they allowed others to take over the tenancy.
translations.idiomatic: People who fled the rebels and abandoned their fields were subject to the usual rule: after half a year their land could be reassigned to new tenants.

sentences.zh: 沆曰：「是豈與凶年詭征役者同科？

translations.literal: Hang said: "How can this be judged the same category as crafty withholding of corvée in a bad year?"
translations.idiomatic: Hang protested, "Surely this is not the same as evading corvée through fraud in a year of disaster?"

sentences.zh: 」奏申其期。

translations.literal: He memorialized to extend the period.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for an extension of the deadline.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、陝西都轉運使，改河北。

translations.literal: He was promoted Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Celestial Manifestations and Grand Transport Commissioner for Shaanxi, then changed to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Hall of Celestial Manifestations and appointed grand transport commissioner for Shaanxi, then transferred to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 李仲昌建六塔河之議，以為費省而功倍。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchang established the proposal for the Six Towers River, holding that expense would be saved while achievement doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchang championed the Six Towers River scheme, claiming it would cost less yet achieve twice the result.

sentences.zh: 詔沆行視，沆言：「近計塞商胡，本度五百八十萬工，用薪芻千六百萬；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hang to go inspect. Hang said: "The recent plan to block Shanghu originally estimated five million eight hundred thousand work units, using fodder and fuel to the tune of sixteen million;"
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Hang to inspect the works in person. Hang reported, "The recent project to dam the Shanghu Reach was originally estimated at 5.8 million work units and 16 million in fodder and fuel;

sentences.zh: 今才用功一萬，薪芻三百萬。

translations.literal: Now only ten thousand work units have been used, fodder and fuel three million.
translations.idiomatic: so far only ten thousand units of labor have been spent, with three million in fodder and fuel.

sentences.zh: 均一河也，而功力不相侔如是，蓋仲昌先為小計，以來興役爾。

translations.literal: It is one and the same river, yet labor and achievement do not match thus—clearly Zhongchang first made a small estimate to launch the project.
translations.idiomatic: It is the same river, yet the figures bear no comparison. Zhongchang obviously lowballed the estimate to get the project started.

sentences.zh: 況所規新渠，視河廣不能五之一，安能容受？

translations.literal: Moreover the new channel he proposes, compared to the river's breadth cannot reach one fifth—how can it receive and hold?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the channel he proposes is less than a fifth the width of the river. How could it possibly hold the volume?

sentences.zh: 此役若成，河必泛溢，齊、博、濱、棣之民其魚矣。

translations.literal: If this work is completed, the river will certainly overflow; the people of Qi, Bo, Bin, and Di will be fish under water.
translations.idiomatic: If this project is finished, the river will inevitably burst its banks. The people of Qi, Bo, Bin, and Di will be drowned like fish in a flood.

sentences.zh: 」既而從初議，河塞復決，如沆言。

translations.literal: Afterward they followed the original proposal; the river dam broke again, just as Hang had said.
translations.idiomatic: The court went ahead with the original plan anyway. The dam failed again, exactly as Hang had warned.

sentences.zh: 又徙河東轉運使，遷龍圖閣直學士、知慶州，召知通進銀臺司、判太常寺。

translations.literal: Again transferred transport commissioner of Hedong, promoted Dragon Diagram Hall Direct Academician and prefect of Qing Prefecture, summoned as director of Transmission and Ectasy Bureau and director of Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to transport commissioner for Hedong, then promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Qingzhou, and finally summoned to head the Bureau for Transmission of Documents and Ectasy and to serve as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 英宗既即位，契丹賀乾元節使至，沆館客，欲取書柩前，使者以非典故，不可。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yingzong had taken the throne, when the Khitan envoy for congratulating the Qianyuan Festival arrived, Hang received him as host. He wished to take the letter before the coffin; the envoy argued it was not precedent and could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong's accession, when the Khitan envoy arrived to offer congratulations on the Qianyuan Festival, Hang received him as chief host. Hang wished to present the letter of condolence before the coffin, but the envoy insisted this was not established precedent.

sentences.zh: 沆折之曰：「昔貴國有喪，吾使至柳河即反，今聽於几筵達命。

translations.literal: Hang rebutted him: "Formerly when your noble state had bereavement, our envoy reached Willow River and turned back at once; today to hear at the bier and deliver the commission—grace and ritual are already thick."
translations.idiomatic: Hang pressed back: "When your court was in mourning, our envoy turned back as soon as he reached Willow River. To let you deliver your message at the imperial bier is already an extraordinary courtesy.

sentences.zh: 恩禮厚矣，尚何云？

translations.literal: Grace and ritual are already thick—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: The honor shown you is more than ample. What objection remains?

sentences.zh: 」使者立授書。

translations.literal: The envoy immediately presented the letter standing.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy at once handed over the letter where he stood.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未知契丹主年，沆乘間雜他語以問，得其實，使者悔之曰：「今復應兄事南朝矣。」

translations.literal: The court did not yet know the Khitan ruler's age. Hang, mixing other talk in an interval, inquired and got the fact. The envoy regretted it, saying: "Now again I must treat the Southern Court as elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: The court did not yet know the Khitan emperor's age. Hang slipped the question into casual conversation and learned the truth. The envoy, realizing his mistake, lamented, "Now I must again acknowledge the Southern Court as elder brother."

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士、知成德軍。

translations.literal: Promoted Direct Academician of Military Affairs Bureau and military commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 俗方棄親事佛。

translations.literal: Local custom was abandoning parents to serve Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom had people abandoning their parents to take Buddhist vows.

sentences.zh: 沆閱按，斥數千人還其家。

translations.literal: Hang reviewed registers and sent several thousand back to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Hang examined the rolls and sent several thousand of them home to their families.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎致仕，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He retired as vice minister of Households due to age; died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as vice minister of the Households and died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李中師

translations.literal: Li Zhongshi
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongshi

sentences.zh: 李中師，字君錫，開封人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongshi, styled Junxi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongshi, whose courtesy name was Junxi, was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，陳執中薦為集賢校理、提點開封府界。

translations.literal: Placed as jinshi; Chen Zhizhong recommended him as Hall of Assembled Worthies collator and regional inspector of Kaifeng prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was recommended by Chen Zhizhong for appointment as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and regional inspector of the Kaifeng prefectural border.

sentences.zh: 境多盜，中師立賞格，督吏分捕，盡得之。

translations.literal: The border had many bandits; Zhongshi established reward scales, pressed officials to hunt in divisions, and got them all.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rife in his jurisdiction. Zhongshi set bounty scales, divided his officers into search teams, and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 進秩，辭不受，乃擢度支判官，為淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: Advanced in rank, he declined to accept; thereupon elevated Revenue Branch judge and made Huainan transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When a promotion was offered, he refused it; he was then appointed a judge in the Revenue Branch and made transport commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 兩浙饑，移淮粟振贍，僚屬議勿與，中師曰：「朝廷視民，淮、浙等爾。

translations.literal: The Two Zhes suffered famine; Huai grain was moved to relieve; subordinates debated not giving; Zhongshi said: "The court regards the people—Huai and Zhe are equal."
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Two Zhes, he was ordered to ship Huainan grain for relief. His staff argued against releasing the stores. Zhongshi said, "In the court's eyes, the people of Huai and Zhe are the same."

sentences.zh: 」卒與之。

translations.literal: In the end he gave it.
translations.idiomatic: He released the grain.

sentences.zh: 徙河東，入為度支副使，拜天章閣待制、陝西都轉運使，知澶州、河南府。

translations.literal: Transferred Hedong, entered as Revenue Branch deputy commissioner, received Hall of Celestial Manifestations Attendant Gentleman and Shaanxi Grand Transport Commissioner, prefect of Chan and Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong, recalled as deputy commissioner of the Revenue Branch, made attendant gentleman of the Hall of Celestial Manifestations and grand transport commissioner for Shaanxi, and served as prefect of Chanzhou and Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召權三司使、龍圖閣直學士，復為河南。

translations.literal: Summoned to act as Three Departments commissioner and Dragon Diagram Hall Direct Academician, again Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as acting commissioner of the Three Departments and direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, then returned again to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前此多大臣居守，委事掾幕，吏習弛緩，中師一以嚴整齊之。

translations.literal: Before this many great ministers held guard and delegated affairs to staff secretaries; clerks had grown lax and slack. Zhongshi brought strict order to all.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, the prefecture had usually been held by senior ministers who left daily business to their staff, and the clerks had grown slack. Zhongshi tightened every detail with rigorous discipline.

sentences.zh: 號為治辦。

translations.literal: He was called efficient in administration.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for running a tight, efficient office.

sentences.zh: 然用法刻深，煩碎無大體，唯厚結中人。

translations.literal: Yet his use of law was harsh and deep, fussy without great principle, only thickly cultivating palace insiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enforced the law with punitive severity and petty fussiness, showing little sense of larger principle, and cultivated palace eunuchs with conspicuous favor.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗嘗對宰相稱其治狀，富弼曰：「陛下何從知之？

translations.literal: At first Shenzong once facing the chancellor praised his governance; Fu Bi said: "Your Majesty from where did you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, Shenzong remarked to his chief minister that Zhongshi governed well. Fu Bi asked, "Your Majesty, how would you know?"

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 中師銜弼沮已，及再至，弼已老，乃籍其戶，令出免役錢與富民等。

translations.literal: Zhongshi resented Bi obstructing himself; when he came again, Bi was already old, so he registered his household and ordered him to pay exemption-service money equal to rich households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshi nursed a grudge against Fu Bi for blocking his reputation. When he returned to Henan, Bi was already advanced in years, and Zhongshi placed his name on the household rolls, requiring him to pay exemption-service fees on the same scale as the wealthiest men.

sentences.zh: 又希司農指，多取餘，視他處為重，洛人怨之。

translations.literal: He also curried Finance Commission favor, over-collecting surpluses, heavier than other places; Luoyang people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He also courted the Finance Commission, extracting heavier surplus levies than anywhere else, and the people of Luoyang bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以中師率先推行，召為群牧使。

translations.literal: Because Zhongshi took the lead in implementing, summoned as Horse Pasture commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhongshi had been foremost in enforcing the new measures, the court summoned him to serve as commissioner of the Directorate of Horse Pastures.

sentences.zh: 乞廢河南、北監牧，省國費，而養馬於民，不報。

translations.literal: He petitioned to abolish Henan and Hebei pasture supervision, save state expense, and raise horses among the people; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to abolish the northern and southern pasture commissions, cut state costs, and shift horse breeding to private households. The throne never answered.

sentences.zh: 後竟行其說，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Later in the end his proposal was enacted; the people could not bear the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In time his plan was adopted anyway, and the common people found it unbearable.

sentences.zh: 權發遣開封府，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Acting provisional dispatcher of Kaifeng Prefecture; died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting chief administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture, he died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 有女嫁陳執中子世儒，坐夫事誅死。

translations.literal: He had a daughter who married Chen Zhizhong's son Shiyru; due to her husband's affair she was executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: He had a daughter who married Chen Zhizhong's son Shiyru; she was put to death when her husband's case brought capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 羅拯，字道濟，祥符人。

translations.literal: Luo Zheng, styled Daoji, was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zheng, styled Daoji, was a native of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 第進士，歷官知榮州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through office, serving as prefect of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through office until he governed Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州介兩江間，每江漲，輒犯城郭，拯作東西二堤除其患。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay between two rivers; whenever the rivers rose, they would breach the city walls. Zheng built eastern and western dikes to remove the harm.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay between two rivers, and whenever they flooded the waters would breach the city walls. Zheng built dikes to the east and west and eliminated the hazard.

sentences.zh: 選知秀州，為江西轉運判官、提點福建刑獄。

translations.literal: He was selected to govern Xiuzhou, served as transport vice-commissioner for Jiangxi, and as judicial intendant for Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected to govern Xiuzhou, then served as Jiangxi transport vice-commissioner and Fujian judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 泉州興化軍水壞廬舍，拯請勿徵海運竹木，經一年，民居皆復其舊。

translations.literal: Floods in Quanzhou and Xinghua Circuit destroyed dwellings. Zheng requested that the maritime-tax levy on bamboo and timber not be collected; after one year, the people's homes all returned to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: When floods in Quanzhou and Xinghua Circuit destroyed dwellings, Zheng asked that the maritime levy on bamboo and timber be suspended. Within a year the people's homes had all been restored.

sentences.zh: 遷轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 邵武之光澤不榷酒，以課賦民，號「黃麹錢」，拯均之他三邑，人以為便。

translations.literal: In Shaowu, Guangze did not monopolize wine but taxed the people under a levy called the "Yellow Ferment Fee." Zheng spread it evenly among the other three counties, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaowu, Guangze did not monopolize wine but taxed the people through a levy called the Yellow Ferment Fee. Zheng spread that burden evenly across the other three counties, and people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 改江、淮發運副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice-director of Jiang-Huai grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as vice-director of Jiang-Huai grain transport.

sentences.zh: 江、淮故無積倉，漕船繫岸下，俟糴入乃得行，蓋官吏以淮南不受陳粟為逃譴計。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai formerly had no reserve granaries; transport boats were tied at shore and could sail only after grain was purchased—officials used Huainan's refusal to accept old grain as a plan to evade censure.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai had no reserve granaries; transport boats had to tie up at shore and wait for fresh purchases before they could sail. Officials had arranged this so that Huainan would not accept old grain, thereby evading accountability.

sentences.zh: 拯始請凡米至而不可上供者，以廩軍；

translations.literal: Zheng first requested that any rice arriving unfit for tribute be issued to garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng first proposed that any grain arriving unfit for tribute be issued to garrison troops;

sentences.zh: 又貯浙西米於潤倉以時運，自是漕增而費省。

translations.literal: He also stored Zhexi rice in Runzhou granaries for timely transport. From then on transport increased while costs were saved.
translations.idiomatic: He also stored Zhexi grain in Runzhou granaries for shipment on schedule. From then on transport volume rose while costs fell.

sentences.zh: 轉為使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 拯使閩時，泉商黃謹往高麗，館之禮賓省，其王云自天聖後職貢絕，欲命使與謹俱來。

translations.literal: While Zheng was commissioner in Min, the Quanzhou merchant Huang Jin went to Goryeo and was lodged at the Ministry of Rites for Hosting Guests. The king said that since the Tiansheng era tribute missions had ceased, he wished to send an envoy to come together with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: While Zheng served in Fujian, the Quanzhou merchant Huang Jin traveled to Goryeo and was lodged at the Ministry of Rites for Hosting Guests. The Goryeo king said that tribute missions had ceased since the Tiansheng era and that he wished to send an envoy to return with Jin.

sentences.zh: 至是，拯以聞，神宗許之，遂遣金悌入貢。

translations.literal: At this point Zheng reported it to the throne; Emperor Shenzong approved, and Jin Ti was then sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng reported this to the throne; Emperor Shenzong approved, and Goryeo then sent Jin Ti to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 高麗復通中國自茲始。

translations.literal: Goryeo's restored contact with China began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo's restored contact with China began from this point.

sentences.zh: 加天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Hanlin Associate at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Hanlin Associate at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.

sentences.zh: 居職七年，徙知永興軍、青、潁、秦三州，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: After seven years in office he was transferred to govern Yongxing Circuit and the three prefectures of Qing, Ying, and Qin. He died at sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in office he was transferred to govern Yongxing Circuit and the prefectures of Qing, Ying, and Qin. He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 拯性和柔，不與人校曲直。

translations.literal: Zheng's nature was gentle and mild; he did not argue right and wrong with others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was gentle by nature and did not quarrel over right and wrong with others.

sentences.zh: 為發運使時，與副皮公弼不協。

translations.literal: When he was transport commissioner, he did not harmonize with his deputy Pi Gongbi.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transport commissioner, he did not get along with his deputy Pi Gongbi.

sentences.zh: 公弼徙他道，御吏劾其貸官錢，拯力為辨理。

translations.literal: Gongbi was transferred to another circuit; imperial censors impeached him for borrowing official funds, and Zheng forcefully argued in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongbi was transferred elsewhere, imperial censors impeached him for borrowing official funds. Zheng forcefully argued in his defense.

sentences.zh: 錢公輔為諫官，嘗論拯短，而公輔姻黨多在拯部內，往往薦進之。

translations.literal: Qian Gongfu, as a remonstrance official, had once criticized Zheng's faults, yet many of Gongfu's relatives and associates were within Zheng's jurisdiction, and Zheng often recommended them for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gongfu, as a remonstrance official, had once criticized Zheng's faults, yet many of Gongfu's relatives and associates fell within Zheng's jurisdiction, and Zheng often recommended them for advancement.

sentences.zh: 或譏以德報怨，拯曰：「同僚不協，所見異也；

translations.literal: Some mocked him for repaying enmity with virtue. Zheng said, "When colleagues fail to harmonize, it is because their views differ;
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked him for repaying enmity with kindness. Zheng said, "When colleagues fail to get along, it is because their views differ;

sentences.zh: 諫官所言，職也。

translations.literal: What a remonstrance official says is his duty.
translations.idiomatic: What a remonstrance official says is his duty.

sentences.zh: 又何怨乎？

translations.literal: Why should I hold a grudge?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I hold a grudge?"

sentences.zh: 」時論服其長者。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion admired him as a man of forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion admired him as a man of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 馬仲甫

translations.literal: Ma Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 馬仲甫，字子山，廬江人，太子少保亮之子也。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongfu, styled Zishan, was a native of Lujiang and the son of the Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Ma Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongfu, styled Zishan, was a native of Lujiang and the son of the Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Ma Liang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，知登封縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Dengfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Dengfeng County.

sentences.zh: 轘轅道險厄，遂傭民鑿平為坦塗，人便其行，為刻石頌美。

translations.literal: The Huanyuan Pass road was perilous and difficult; he hired laborers to cut and level it into a smooth track. People found travel easy and erected a stone monument in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Huanyuan Pass road was perilous and treacherous, so he hired laborers to cut and level it into a smooth track. Travelers found the route easy, and they erected a stone monument in praise.

sentences.zh: 通判趙州，知台州，為度支判官。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Zhao Prefecture, prefect of Taizhou, and finance vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Zhao Prefecture, prefect of Taizhou, and finance vice-commissioner.

sentences.zh: 內侍楊永德言漕舟淮、汴間，惟水遞鋪為便。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Yang Yongde said that for transport boats between the Huai and Bian rivers, using only water courier stations would be most convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Yang Yongde proposed that for transport boats between the Huai and Bian rivers, relying only on water courier stations would be most convenient.

sentences.zh: 詔仲甫偕往訂可否，還言其害十餘條，議遂格。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhongfu to go with him to assess the proposal. On returning he listed more than ten harms, and the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhongfu to accompany him and assess the proposal. On returning, Zhongfu listed more than ten harms, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 出為夔路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as transport commissioner for the Kui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as transport commissioner for Kui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，盜粟者當論死，仲甫請罪減一等，詔須奏裁。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, grain thieves were liable to the death penalty. Zhongfu requested that the offense be reduced one grade; the edict required submission for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine, grain thieves were liable to the death penalty. Zhongfu requested that the offense be reduced one grade, but the edict required that this be submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 復言：「饑羸拘囚，比得報，死矣，請決而後奏。」

translations.literal: He said again, "The starving and feeble are detained in prison; by the time a reply arrives, they will be dead. I ask leave to decide first and report afterward."
translations.idiomatic: He said again, "The starving and feeble are held in prison; by the time a reply arrives, they will be dead. I ask leave to decide first and report afterward."

sentences.zh: 徙使淮南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner for Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 真、揚諸州地狹，出米少，官糴之多，價常踴登，濱江米狼戾，而農無所售。

translations.literal: Zhen, Yang, and other prefectures had narrow territory and produced little rice, yet official purchases were heavy, so prices always spiked. Along the river, rice lay abundant and unsold, while farmers found no buyers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Yang, and neighboring prefectures had little land and produced little rice, yet official purchases there were heavy and prices always soared. Along the river rice lay abundant and unsold, while farmers had no one to sell to.

sentences.zh: 仲甫請移糴以紓其患，兩益於民，從之。

translations.literal: Zhongfu requested shifting purchases to relieve the problem, benefiting both regions; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu requested shifting purchases elsewhere to relieve the problem, a change that would benefit both regions. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 遂繇戶部判官為發運使。

translations.literal: He then rose from finance vice-commissioner to transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose from finance vice-commissioner to transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自淮陰徑泗上浮長淮，風波覆舟，歲罹其患。

translations.literal: From Huaiyin one went straight up the Si River onto the Long Huai; storms capsized boats every year.
translations.idiomatic: From Huaiyin boats went straight up the Si River onto the Long Huai, where storms capsized them year after year.

sentences.zh: 仲甫建議鑿洪澤渠六十里，漕者便之。

translations.literal: Zhongfu proposed excavating a sixty-li channel at Hongze Lake, which greatly eased transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu proposed excavating a sixty-li channel at Hongze Lake, and transport crews found the route much easier.

sentences.zh: 拜天章閣待制、知瀛州秦州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Associate at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and assigned as prefect of Ying and Qin Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Associate at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and assigned to govern Ying and Qin Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 古渭介青唐之南，夏人在其北，中通一徑，小警則路絕。

translations.literal: Guwei lay south of Qingtang; Tangut people were to its north. A single narrow path ran through the middle; at the slightest alarm the route was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Guwei lay south of Qingtang with Tangut people to the north. Only one narrow path ran between them, and at the slightest alarm the route was cut off.

sentences.zh: 仲甫得篳栗城故址，自雞川砦築堡，北抵南谷，環數百里為內地，詔賜名甘谷堡。

translations.literal: Zhongfu took the old site of Bili Fort, built a bastion from Jichuan Stockade north to Nangu Valley, enclosed several hundred li as interior territory, and the court bestowed the name Gangu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu took the old site of Bili Fort and built a bastion from Jichuan Stockade north to Nangu Valley, enclosing several hundred li as interior territory. The court bestowed on it the name Gangu Fort.

sentences.zh: 故時羌人入城貿易，皆僦邸，仲甫設館處之，陽示禮厚，實閑之也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Qiang traders entered the city to trade, they all rented inns. Zhongfu established guesthouses to lodge them—outwardly showing generous courtesy, but in fact keeping them under restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Qiang traders entered the city to trade, they all rented inns. Zhongfu established guesthouses to lodge them, outwardly showing generous courtesy while in fact keeping them under restraint.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，守亳、許、揚三州，糾察在京刑獄，知通進銀臺司，復為揚州，提舉崇禧觀，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era he governed Bo, Xu, and Yang Prefectures, inspected capital prisons, directed the Memorial Chancellery and Silver Terrace Office, returned to Yangzhou, was put in charge of the Chongxi Abbey, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era he governed Bo, Xu, and Yang Prefectures, inspected capital prisons, directed the Memorial Chancellery and Silver Terrace Office, returned to Yangzhou, was put in charge of the Chongxi Abbey, and died.

sentences.zh: 王居卿

translations.literal: Wang Juqing
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juqing

sentences.zh: 王居卿，字壽明，登州蓬萊人，以進士至知齊州，提舉夔路京東刑獄、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Wang Juqing, styled Shouming, was a native of Penglai in Deng Prefecture. Passing the jinshi examination, he rose to prefect of Qi Prefecture, judicial intendant for the Kui and Jingdong Circuits, and salt-and-iron vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juqing, styled Shouming, was a native of Penglai in Deng Prefecture. After passing the jinshi examination he rose to prefect of Qi Prefecture, judicial intendant for Kui and Jingdong Circuits, and salt-and-iron vice-commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建言商賈轉百貨市塞上者，聽以家貲抵於官，為給長券，至賣所，並輸徵稅直，公私便之。

translations.literal: He proposed that merchants transporting goods to sell at the frontier be allowed to pledge household assets with the government in exchange for long-term vouchers; at the place of sale they would pay the tax value together—convenient for both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that merchants transporting goods to sell on the frontier be allowed to pledge household assets with the government in exchange for long-term vouchers, then pay the full tax at the place of sale. Both public and private interests would benefit.

sentences.zh: 出知揚州，改京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Yangzhou, then transferred to transport commissioner for Jingdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Yangzhou, then transferred to transport commissioner for Jingdong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 青州河貫城中，苦泛溢為病，居卿即城立飛梁，上設樓櫓，下建門，以時閉啟，人誦其智。

translations.literal: In Qing Prefecture a river ran through the city, and flooding had long been a scourge. Juqing built a flying bridge over the city wall, set watch towers above and gates below, opening and closing them according to season. People praised his ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing Prefecture a river ran through the city, and flooding had long been a scourge. Juqing built a flying bridge atop the city wall, with watch towers above and gates below that opened and closed according to season. People praised his ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 徙河北路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，居卿立軟橫二埽以遏怒流，而不與水爭。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst at Caocun, Juqing erected two soft transverse embankments to check the raging current without fighting the water head-on.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Caocun, Juqing erected two soft transverse embankments to check the raging current without fighting the water head-on.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞其功，建以為都水法。

translations.literal: The court rewarded his achievement and established his method as standard hydraulics practice.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded his achievement and made his method standard practice for the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 召拜戶部副使、提舉市易，擢天章閣待制、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed vice-minister of revenue and commissioner for the market-trade monopoly, then promoted to Hanlin Associate and chief transport commissioner for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed vice-minister of revenue and commissioner for the market-trade monopoly, then promoted to Hanlin Associate and chief transport commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 知秦州、太原府，卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He governed Qin Prefecture and Taiyuan Prefecture, and died at sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qin Prefecture and Taiyuan Prefecture, and died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 居卿俗吏，特以言利至從官。

translations.literal: Juqing was a vulgar bureaucrat who rose to high office solely through profit-seeking proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Juqing was a vulgar bureaucrat who rose to high office solely through proposals for profit.

sentences.zh: 孫構字紹先，博平人。

translations.literal: Sun Gou, styled Shaoxian, was a native of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gou, styled Shaoxian, was a native of Boping.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，為廣濟軍判官，歲入圭田粟六百石，構止受百石，餘以畀學官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as vice-magistrate of Guangji Circuit. The annual income from official fields was six hundred shi of grain; Gou accepted only one hundred shi and gave the rest to the school officials.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as vice-magistrate of Guangji Circuit. The official fields yielded six hundred shi of grain each year; Gou accepted only one hundred shi and gave the rest to the school officials.

sentences.zh: 久之，知黎州，夷年墨數擾邊，用間殺之。

translations.literal: After some time he was prefect of Li Prefecture. The Yi chieftain Nianmo repeatedly harried the border; Gou used agents to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became prefect of Li Prefecture. The Yi chieftain Nianmo repeatedly harried the border, and Gou used agents to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 蜀帥呂公弼上其事，擢知真州。

translations.literal: The Sichuan commander Lü Gongbi reported this matter, and Gou was promoted to prefect of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan commander Lü Gongbi reported the affair, and Gou was promoted to prefect of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凶歲得盜，令各指黨伍，悉置諸法，境內為清。

translations.literal: In a bad year he captured thieves, made each one identify his accomplices, and punished them all according to law; the territory was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In a bad year he captured thieves, made each identify his accomplices, and punished them all according to law until the territory was cleared.

sentences.zh: 遷度支判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to finance vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to finance vice-commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夔州部夷梁承秀、李光吉、王兗導生獠入寇，轉運判官張詵請誅之。

translations.literal: In Qizhou Circuit, the Yi leaders Liang Chengxiu, Li Guangji, and Wang Yan led raw Liao raiders in invasion. Transport vice-commissioner Zhang Shen requested their execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Qizhou Circuit, the Yi leaders Liang Chengxiu, Li Guangji, and Wang Yan led raw Liao raiders in invasion. Transport vice-commissioner Zhang Shen requested their execution.

sentences.zh: 選構為使，倍道之官，至則遣渝州豪杜安行募千人往襲，自督官軍及黔中兵擊其後，斬承秀，入討二族，火其居。

translations.literal: Gou was selected as commissioner and rushed to his post by forced marches. On arrival he sent the Yu Prefecture strongman Du Anxing to recruit a thousand men for a surprise attack, while he personally led government troops and Qianzhong forces to strike from the rear. Chengxiu was beheaded; he invaded to punish the other two clans and burned their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was selected as commissioner and rushed to his post by forced marches. On arrival he sent the Yu Prefecture strongman Du Anxing to recruit a thousand men for a surprise attack, while he personally led government troops and Qianzhong forces to strike from the rear. Chengxiu was beheaded; Gou then invaded to punish the other two clans and burned their dwellings.

sentences.zh: 餘眾保黑崖嶺，黔兵從間道夜譟而進，光吉墜崖死，兗自縛降。

translations.literal: The survivors held Black Cliff Ridge. Qianzhong troops advanced by a hidden path at night with loud clamor; Guangji fell from a cliff and died, and Yan bound himself and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors held Black Cliff Ridge. Qianzhong troops advanced by a hidden path at night with loud clamor; Guangji fell from a cliff and died, and Yan bound himself and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以其地建南平軍。

translations.literal: On this territory was established Nanping Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On this territory Nanping Military Prefecture was established.

sentences.zh: 錄功加直昭文館。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was given direct appointment to the Hall for Cherishing Literary Works.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and he was given direct appointment to the Hall for Cherishing Literary Works.

sentences.zh: 徙湖北轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner for Hubei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for Hubei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 章惇興南、北江蠻事，構諭降懿、洽二州，納歸附州十四。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun launched the southern and northern Jiang barbarian campaigns, Gou persuaded Yi and Qia Prefectures to submit and brought in fourteen surrendering prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun launched the southern and northern Jiang barbarian campaigns, Gou persuaded Yi and Qia Prefectures to submit and brought in fourteen surrendering prefectures.

sentences.zh: 初，渡辰溪，舟毀而溺，得援者僅免，神宗憫之，賜帛三百。

translations.literal: Earlier, crossing the Chen River, his boat was wrecked and he nearly drowned; only with rescue did he barely escape. Emperor Shenzong took pity and granted him three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, crossing the Chen River, his boat was wrecked and he nearly drowned; only with rescue did he barely escape. Emperor Shenzong took pity on him and granted him three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 北江酋彭師晏常持向背，構知向水酋彭儒武與有隙，檄使攻之。

translations.literal: The northern Jiang chieftain Peng Shiyan often wavered in allegiance. Gou knew that Xiangshui chieftain Peng Ruwu bore a grudge against him and issued an order for Ruwu to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The northern Jiang chieftain Peng Shiyan often wavered in allegiance. Gou knew that the Xiangshui chieftain Peng Ruwu bore a grudge against him and ordered Ruwu to attack.

sentences.zh: 師晏降，得其下溪州地，五溪皆平。

translations.literal: Shiyan surrendered; Gou obtained the territory of Xi Prefecture, and the Five Streams region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan surrendered; Gou obtained the territory of Xi Prefecture, and the Five Streams region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進集賢殿修撰，賜三品服。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and granted third-rank official robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and granted third-rank official robes.

sentences.zh: 交阯入寇，拜右諫議大夫、知桂州，聲言將掎角搗其巢穴，寇聞引去。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi invaded, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Gui Prefecture. He publicly declared he would coordinate a pincer attack on their nest; hearing this, the invaders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi invaded, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Gui Prefecture. He publicly declared that he would coordinate a pincer attack on their stronghold, and the invaders withdrew at the news.

sentences.zh: 以疾提舉崇福宮，換太中大夫，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Ill, he was put in charge of the Chongfu Palace, exchanged his post for Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and died at sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he was put in charge of the Chongfu Palace, exchanged his post for Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 構喜功名，勇於建立，西南邊事自此始云。

translations.literal: Gou loved fame and achievement and was bold in establishing new projects; the southwestern frontier campaigns are said to have begun with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou loved fame and achievement and was bold in establishing new projects; the southwestern frontier campaigns are said to have begun with him.

sentences.zh: 張詵，字樞言，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shen, styled Shuyan, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shen, styled Shuyan, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，通判越州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as vice-prefect of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as vice-prefect of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民患苦衙前役，詵科別人戶，籍其當役者，以差人錢為雇人充，皆以為便。

translations.literal: The people suffered under the yamen-runner corvée. Shen classified separate household categories, registered those liable for service, and used dispatch fees to hire substitutes—everyone found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered under the yamen-runner corvée. Shen classified separate household categories, registered those liable for service, and used dispatch fees to hire substitutes. Everyone found the arrangement convenient.

sentences.zh: 知襄邑縣，擢夔路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Xiangyi County and was promoted to transport vice-commissioner for Kui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Xiangyi County and was promoted to transport vice-commissioner for Kui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 錄辟土之功，加直集賢院，改陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: His merit in opening territory was recorded; he was given direct appointment to the Hall of Assembled Worthies and transferred to vice-transport commissioner for Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in opening territory was recorded; he was given direct appointment to the Hall of Assembled Worthies and transferred to vice-transport commissioner for Shaanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 召對，帝曰：「朕未識卿，每閱章奏，獨卿與蔡挺有所論請，使人了然。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor said, "I do not yet know you personally, but whenever I review memorials, only you and Cai Ting submit proposals that are immediately clear.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, the emperor said, "I do not yet know you personally, but whenever I review memorials, only you and Cai Ting submit proposals that are immediately clear.

sentences.zh: 尋當以帥事相屬。

translations.literal: Before long I shall entrust you with military command."
translations.idiomatic: Before long I shall entrust you with military command."

sentences.zh: 」及入辭，賜服金紫。

translations.literal: When he came to take leave, he was granted gold-and-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave, he was granted gold-and-purple robes.

sentences.zh: 明年，直龍圖閣、知秦州。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed direct at the Hall of Dragon Imprints and prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed direct at the Hall of Dragon Imprints and prefect of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前此將吏貪功，多從羌地獵射，因起邊患。

translations.literal: Before this, officers and officials, greedy for merit, had often hunted in Qiang territory, thereby provoking border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, officers and officials greedy for merit had often hunted in Qiang territory, thereby provoking border trouble.

sentences.zh: 詵至，申令毋得犯，得一人，斬諸境上，群羌感悅，遷天章閣待制、知熙州。

translations.literal: When Shen arrived, he issued orders forbidding encroachment; one offender was caught and executed at the border. The Qiang tribes were moved and pleased. He was transferred to Hanlin Associate and prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen arrived, he issued orders forbidding encroachment; one offender was caught and executed at the border. The Qiang tribes were moved and pleased. He was transferred to Hanlin Associate and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 董氈遣鬼章逼岷州，詵往討，董氈迎戰，破之於錯鑿城，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: Dongzhan sent Guizhang to press Min Prefecture. Shen went to suppress him; Dongzhan came out to fight and was defeated at Cuozao Fort, with ten thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhan sent Guizhang to press Min Prefecture. Shen went to suppress him; Dongzhan came out to fight and was defeated at Cuozao Fort, with ten thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，加龍圖閣直學士、知成都府，徙杭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was made Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Imprints and prefect of Chengdu, then transferred to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was made Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Imprints and prefect of Chengdu, then transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，復命權經略熙河事，趣使倍道行。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he was again ordered to hold acting authority over frontier affairs in Xihe Circuit and urged to travel by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, he was again ordered to hold acting authority over frontier affairs in Xihe Circuit and urged to travel by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 時倉卒治戎，有司計產調夫，戶至累首，民多流亡。

translations.literal: At the time military preparations were rushed; agencies assessed property and levied corvée labor, families burdened head upon head, and many people fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military preparations were rushed; agencies assessed property and levied corvée labor until families were burdened head upon head, and many people fled.

sentences.zh: 詵中塗訴其狀，乞敕劍外招攜之，不報。

translations.literal: En route Shen reported the situation, begging an edict to recall and resettle those beyond Jianmen Pass; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: En route Shen reported the situation, begging an edict to recall and resettle those beyond Jianmen Pass. No reply came.

sentences.zh: 會靈武師罷，乃赴杭，道過京師，帝訪以西事，對曰：「彼勢雖弱，而我師未銳，邊備未飭，願以歲月圖功。

translations.literal: When the Lingwu campaign was called off, he proceeded to Hangzhou. Passing through the capital, the emperor questioned him on western affairs. He answered, "Their power may be weak, but our army is not yet sharp, nor are border defenses in order; I wish to achieve success over months and years."
translations.idiomatic: When the Lingwu campaign was called off, he proceeded to Hangzhou. Passing through the capital, the emperor questioned him on western affairs. He answered, "Their power may be weak, but our army is not yet sharp and border defenses are not in order. I wish to achieve success over months and years."

sentences.zh: 」累官正議大夫，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Righteousness Grandee and died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to Righteousness Grandee and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詵性孝友，廉於財，平生不殖田業。

translations.literal: Shen was filial and brotherly by nature, scrupulous with money, and never accumulated farmland in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was filial and brotherly by nature, scrupulous with money, and never accumulated farmland in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 既建拓瀘夷地被進用後，雖有善言可紀，終不逭清議云。

translations.literal: After he was promoted for opening and expanding territory among the Luo tribes of Luzhou, though commendable words might be recorded of him, he could never entirely escape censure in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: After he was promoted for opening and expanding territory among the Luo tribes of Luzhou, though commendable words might be recorded of him, he could never entirely escape censure in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 蘇寀，字公佐，磁州滏陽人。

translations.literal: Su Shen, styled Gongzuo, was a native of Fuyang in Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shen, styled Gongzuo, was a native of Fuyang in Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢第，調兗州觀察推官，受知於守杜衍。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations, was assigned as investigative assistant in Yan Prefecture, and won the esteem of the prefect Du Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations, was assigned as investigative assistant in Yan Prefecture, and won the esteem of the prefect Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 為大理詳斷官。

translations.literal: He served as detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served as detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 民有母改嫁而死，既葬，輒盜其柩歸祔，法當死。

translations.literal: A commoner had a mother who remarried and died; after burial he promptly stole her coffin to return it for enshrinement with his father. By law he should die.
translations.idiomatic: A man whose mother had remarried and died stole her coffin after burial so he could enshrine her with his father. The law called for the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 寀曰：「子取母祔父，豈與發塚取財等？

translations.literal: Shen said: "A son taking his mother to be enshrined with his father—how is that the same as opening a grave to seize property?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen said, "A son who moves his mother's remains to lie beside his father's—is that the same as robbing a tomb for profit?"

sentences.zh: 」請而生之。

translations.literal: He petitioned and had the sentence commuted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the throne and had the death sentence commuted.

sentences.zh: 遷審刑院詳議、御史臺推真官，知單州，提點梓州益州路刑獄、利路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to detail deliberator at the Court of Review and verification officer at the Censorate, served as prefect of Shanzhou, judicial intendant for the Zizhou-Yizhou circuit, and transport commissioner for the Lizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to detail deliberator at the Court of Review and verification officer at the Censorate, appointed prefect of Shanzhou, judicial intendant for the Zizhou-Yizhou circuit, and transport commissioner for the Lizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 文州歲市羌馬，羌轉買蜀貨，猾駔上下物價，肆為奸漁。

translations.literal: Each year Wenzhou purchased Qiang horses in the market; the Qiang would turn and buy Shu goods, and crafty brokers manipulated prices up and down, freely committing fraud and extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Wen Prefecture purchased Qiang horses at market. The Qiang would resell them to buy Shu goods, while shrewd brokers manipulated prices and freely committed fraud and extortion.

sentences.zh: 寀議置折博務，平貨直以易馬，宿弊頓絕。

translations.literal: Shen proposed establishing barter offices, leveling goods at fair value to exchange for horses, and longstanding abuses ceased at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shen proposed setting up barter offices to exchange goods at fair value for horses, and longstanding abuses were eliminated at once.

sentences.zh: 入判大理寺，為湖北、淮南、成都路轉運使，擢侍御史知雜事，判刑部。

translations.literal: He entered as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, served as transport commissioner for the Hubei, Huainan, and Chengdu circuits, was promoted to secretariat censor with concurrent duties, and served as vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, served as transport commissioner for the Hubei, Huainan, and Chengdu circuits, was promoted to secretariat censor with concurrent duties, and served as vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還及半道，聞英宗晏駕，契丹置宴仍用樂，寀謂送者曰：「兩朝兄第國家，君臣之義，吾與君等一也。

translations.literal: On embassy to the Khitan, halfway back he heard that Emperor Yingzong had passed away. The Khitan set a banquet and still used music. Shen said to those seeing him off: "Our two courts are brother states. In the obligation between ruler and subject, you and I are the same.
translations.idiomatic: While returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he heard halfway that Emperor Yingzong had died. The Khitan still held a banquet with music. Shen said to those escorting him, "Our two courts are brother states. In the bond between ruler and subject, you and I are alike.

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可忍。

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be endured, what cannot be endured?"

sentences.zh: 」遂為之徹樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had the music withdrawn for them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the music stopped for them.

sentences.zh: 進度支副使，以集賢殿修撰知鳳翔。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice commissioner of the Revenue Commission and, as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Worthies, served as prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Revenue Commission and appointed prefect of Fengxiang as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Worthies.

sentences.zh: 還，糾察在京刑獄，又出知潭州、廣州，累轉給事中，知河南府，無留訟。

translations.literal: On his return he supervised capital criminal cases, then was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou and Guangzhou, was repeatedly promoted to chief remonstrance official, and served as prefect of Henan, where no lawsuits lingered.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he supervised criminal cases in the capital, then served as prefect of Tanzhou and Guangzhou, rose to chief remonstrance official, and was appointed prefect of Henan, where no lawsuits lingered.

sentences.zh: 入知審刑院，卒。

translations.literal: He entered as director of the Court of Review and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Court of Review and died in office.

sentences.zh: 寀長於刑名，故屢為法官，數以讞議受詔獎焉。

translations.literal: Shen excelled in criminal law, hence repeatedly served as a judge, and several times received imperial commendation for legal deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen excelled in criminal law and was repeatedly appointed a judge. Several times he received imperial commendation for his legal deliberations.

sentences.zh: 馬從先

translations.literal: Ma Congxian
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congxian

sentences.zh: 馬從先，字子野，祥符人。

translations.literal: Ma Congxian, styled Ziye, was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congxian, courtesy name Ziye, was a native of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 少盡力於學。

translations.literal: In youth he exerted himself fully in study.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he applied himself wholeheartedly to learning.

sentences.zh: 父當任子，推以與其弟。

translations.literal: When his father was entitled to an hereditary appointment for a son, he yielded it to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was entitled to appoint a son to office by privilege, he yielded the appointment to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 由進士累官太常少卿、知宿州。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through the jinshi degree he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 宿在淮、汴間，素難治，從先以囊博者、重坐者厚賞以求盜。

translations.literal: Suzhou lay between the Huai and Bian rivers and had always been hard to govern. Congxian offered heavy rewards to gamblers and repeat offenders to catch thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou lay between the Huai and Bian rivers and had long been difficult to govern. Congxian offered heavy rewards to gamblers and repeat offenders for information leading to the capture of thieves.

sentences.zh: 禁屠牛、鑄錢，嚴甚。

translations.literal: He banned cattle slaughter and coin counterfeiting, enforcing the ban strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly banned cattle slaughter and counterfeiting of coins.

sentences.zh: 大水，發廩振流亡，全活數十萬。

translations.literal: In a great flood he opened granaries to relieve displaced people, and hundreds of thousands were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: During a great flood he opened granaries to relieve displaced people, saving hundreds of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 代還，知壽州，以老辭，英宗諭遣之曰：「聞卿治行籍甚，壽尤重於宿，姑為朕往。

translations.literal: Relieved and returned, he was appointed prefect of Shouzhou. He pleaded old age, but Emperor Yingzong personally urged him, saying: "I hear your record of governance is outstanding. Shouzhou is even weightier than Suzhou—go for me for now.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his term he was appointed prefect of Shouzhou. He pleaded old age, but Emperor Yingzong personally urged him, saying, "I hear your record of governance is outstanding. Shouzhou is an even heavier assignment than Suzhou—go there for me for now."

sentences.zh: 」既至，治如曩時。

translations.literal: Once there, he governed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he governed as ably as before.

sentences.zh: 由太子賓客轉工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: From Palace Mentor he transferred to Vice Minister of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from Palace Mentor to Vice Minister of Works and then retired.

sentences.zh: 從先性整嚴，雖盛夏不袒跣。

translations.literal: Congxian's nature was ordered and strict; even in midsummer he never bared his shoulders or went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Congxian was orderly and strict in character; even in midsummer he never went barefoot or with bared shoulders.

sentences.zh: 晚學佛，預言其終時，年七十六而卒。

translations.literal: Late in life he studied Buddhism, predicted the time of his end, and died at seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he studied Buddhism, foretold the time of his death, and died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 論曰：長卿性務廉潔，以能臣稱，中師用法刻深，以治辨稱，雖均為材吏，而優劣自見。

translations.literal: Commentary: Zhangqing's nature was devoted to integrity and he gained fame as a capable minister. Zhongshi applied the law harshly and deeply and was famed for governance and judgment. Though both were talented officials, their relative merit and demerit show for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhangqing devoted himself to integrity and was praised as a capable minister. Zhongshi applied the law harshly and was famed for his governance and judgment. Though both were talented officials, their relative strengths and weaknesses are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 拯及仲甫俱能為國興利除害。

translations.literal: Zheng and Zhongfu were both able to bring benefit to the state and remove harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Zhongfu were both able to bring benefit to the state and remove harm from it.

sentences.zh: 構始開西南邊，詵遂拓瀘夷被進用，雖有他善，而不能逭清議。

translations.literal: Gou first opened the southwest frontier, and Shen then expanded Luzhou barbarian territory and was promoted. Though they had other virtues, they could not escape censure from upright opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Gou first opened the southwest frontier, and Shen then expanded the Luzhou Yi territories and was promoted. Though they had other virtues, they could not escape censure from upright opinion.

sentences.zh: 至於沆決河議，綏遠民，折鄰使，歷有可稱述者，其最優歟。

translations.literal: As for Hang's decisions on the Yellow River, reassuring distant peoples, and reining in neighboring envoys, through all these there were things worth recounting. Was he perhaps the finest?
translations.idiomatic: As for Hang's decisions on the Yellow River, his reassurance of distant peoples, and his handling of neighboring envoys, there were accomplishments worth recounting at every turn. Was he perhaps the finest of them all?

sentences.zh: 沈遘，字文通，錢塘人，以蔭為郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: Shen Gou, styled Wentong, was a man of Qiantang. Through yin privilege he became hall officer for suburban and altar rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Gou, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Qiantang. Through yin privilege he was appointed hall officer for suburban and altar rites.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，廷唱第一，大臣謂已官者不得先多士，乃以遘為第二。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and ranked first at the palace announcement, but grand counsellors held that one already holding office could not rank ahead of all scholars, so Gou was placed second.
