translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and ranked first at the palace announcement, but grand counsellors held that one already holding office could not rank ahead of all the scholars, so Gou was placed second.

sentences.zh: 通判江寧府，歸，奏《本治論》。

translations.literal: As assistant prefect of Jiangning he returned and memorialized On Fundamental Governance.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as assistant prefect of Jiangning he returned and submitted On Fundamental Governance.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「近獻文者率以詩賦，豈若此十篇之書為可用也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "Those submitting writings lately have mostly sent poetry and fu—how can that compare with this work of ten chapters in usefulness?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "Those submitting writings lately have mostly sent poetry and rhapsodies—how can that compare with the usefulness of this work in ten chapters?"

sentences.zh: 」除集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，修起居注，遂知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he became compiler of the daily records and then draft edict officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became compiler of the daily records and then draft edict officer.

sentences.zh: 以父扶坐事免，求知越州，徙杭州。

translations.literal: Because his father Fu was implicated and dismissed, he requested appointment as prefect of Yuezhou and was transferred to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Fu was implicated and dismissed, he requested appointment as prefect of Yuezhou and was transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人疏雋博達，明於吏治，令行禁止。

translations.literal: As a man he was open, brilliant, and broad in knowledge, clear in administration—orders were enforced and prohibitions heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Open, brilliant, and broad in knowledge, he was skilled in administration; his orders were enforced and his prohibitions obeyed.

sentences.zh: 民或貧不能葬，給以公錢，嫁孤女數百人，倡優養良家子者，奪歸其父母。

translations.literal: When commoners were too poor to bury their dead he gave public funds; he married off hundreds of orphaned girls; where entertainers kept daughters of respectable families, he took them back to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners were too poor to bury their dead he supplied public funds; he married off hundreds of orphaned girls; and where entertainers kept daughters of respectable families, he had them returned to their parents.

sentences.zh: 善遇僚寀，皆甘樂傾盡為之耳目，刺閭巷長短，纖悉必知，事來立斷。

translations.literal: He treated subordinates well; all gladly gave their utmost as his eyes and ears, probing neighborhood affairs great and small until nothing escaped him, and when matters arose he decided them at once.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his subordinates well, and they gladly served as his eyes and ears throughout the neighborhoods, reporting even the smallest matters until nothing escaped him. When business arose he decided it at once.

sentences.zh: 禁捕西湖魚鱉，故人居湖上，蟹夜入其籬間，適有客會宿，相與食之，旦詣府，遘迎語曰：「昨夜食蟹美乎？

translations.literal: He banned fishing for fish and turtles in West Lake. An old resident lived on the lake; crabs at night entered his fence. A guest happened to stay and they ate them together. At dawn he went to the prefectural office, and Gou met him and said: "Was the crab you ate last night good?
translations.idiomatic: He banned fishing in West Lake. An old resident on the lake found crabs in his fence one night; a guest happened to be staying and they ate them together. At dawn the man went to the prefectural office, and Gou greeted him with, "Was the crab you ate last night good?"

sentences.zh: 」客笑而謝之。

translations.literal: The guest laughed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The guest laughed and apologized.

sentences.zh: 小民有犯法，情稍不善者，不問法輕重，輒刺為兵，奸猾屏息。

translations.literal: When petty commoners violated the law and the circumstances were somewhat bad, regardless of legal severity he would tattoo them as soldiers, and scoundrels fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: When petty offenders broke the law under circumstances that seemed somewhat serious, he tattooed them for military service regardless of the legal penalty, and scoundrels fell silent.

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄鞫真卿將按其狀，遘為稍弛，而刺者復為民。

translations.literal: Judicial intendant Ju Zhenqing was about to investigate on that basis; Gou relaxed the policy somewhat, and those tattooed became commoners again.
translations.idiomatic: When judicial intendant Ju Zhenqing was about to investigate the practice, Gou relaxed it somewhat, and those who had been tattooed were restored to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐遺詔至，為次於外，不飲酒食肉者二十七日。

translations.literal: When the Jiayou testamentary edict arrived, he observed mourning outside, abstaining from wine and meat for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiayou testamentary edict arrived, he observed mourning outside the capital, abstaining from wine and meat for twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 召知開封府，遷龍圖閣直學士，治如在杭州。

translations.literal: He was summoned as prefect of Kaifeng, promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures, and governed as he had at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as prefect of Kaifeng, promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures, and governed as ably as he had at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蚤作視事，逮午而畢，出與親舊還往，從容燕笑，沛然有餘暇，士大夫交稱其能。

translations.literal: He rose early to handle affairs and finished by noon; then he went out to visit kin and friends, at ease in banter and laughter, abundantly with spare time, and scholar-officials universally praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early to transact business and finished by noon, then went out to visit kin and friends at ease in conversation and laughter, with time to spare. Scholar-officials universally praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士、判流內銓。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician and concurrently director of the inner bureau of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Academician and concurrently director of the inner bureau of appointments.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，英宗閔其去，賚黃金百兩，仍命扶喪歸蘇州。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother, Emperor Yingzong pitied his departure, bestowed one hundred taels of gold, and ordered him to escort the coffin home to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, Emperor Yingzong pitied his departure, bestowed one hundred taels of gold, and ordered him to escort the coffin home to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 既葬，廬墓下，服未竟而卒，年四十，世咨惜之。

translations.literal: After burial he lived by the tomb; before mourning ended he died at forty, and the world lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he lived by the tomb, but before mourning ended he died at forty. The world mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 弟遼，從弟括。

translations.literal: Younger brother Liao; younger cousin Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Liao; his younger cousin was Kuo.

sentences.zh: 弟 遼

translations.literal: Younger Brother Liao
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Liao

sentences.zh: 遼，字睿達，幼挺拔不群，長而好學尚友，傲睨一世。

translations.literal: Liao, styled Ruida, was uncommonly outstanding in youth; grown, he loved learning and honored friends, looking down on the age with disdain.
translations.idiomatic: Liao, courtesy name Ruida, was unusually gifted as a boy. Grown, he loved learning and honored friends, and looked down on the world with disdain.

sentences.zh: 讀左氏、班固書，小摹仿之。

translations.literal: Reading Zuo's Commentary and Ban Gu's histories, he would briefly imitate them.
translations.idiomatic: When he read Zuo's Commentary and Ban Gu's histories, he would briefly imitate them.

sentences.zh: 輒近似，乃鋤植縱舍，自成一家。

translations.literal: Soon he came close, then uprooted and planted anew, letting go freely and forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: When he came too close to them, he would uproot his imitation and start afresh, letting go freely until he formed a style of his own.

sentences.zh: 趣操高爽，縹縹然有物外意，絕不喜進取。

translations.literal: His tastes were lofty and unburdened, ethereal with the air of one beyond worldly things, and he utterly disliked advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His tastes were lofty and unburdened, with an ethereal air of one beyond worldly things, and he utterly disliked seeking office.

sentences.zh: 用兄任監壽州酒稅。

translations.literal: Through his brother's appointment he supervised the Shouzhou wine tax.
translations.idiomatic: Through his brother's appointment he supervised the Shouzhou wine tax.

sentences.zh: 吳充使三司，薦監內藏庫。

translations.literal: When Wu Chong headed the Fiscal Commission, he recommended him to supervise the Inner Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Chong headed the Fiscal Commission, he recommended Liao to supervise the Inner Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，分審官建西院，以為主簿，時方重此官，出則奉使持節。

translations.literal: Early in the Xining era the Branch Court of Review established the Western Office and made him registrar. At the time this post was weighty, and going out one served as envoy bearing credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era the Branch Court of Review established the Western Office and made him registrar. The post was then highly valued, and its holder, when sent out, served as envoy bearing credentials.

sentences.zh: 遼故受知於王安石，安石嘗與詩，有「風流謝安石，瀟灑陶淵明」之稱。

translations.literal: Liao had long been favored by Wang Anshi. Anshi once wrote him a poem with the praise "graceful as Xie Anshi, free-spirited as Tao Yuanming."
translations.idiomatic: Liao had long been favored by Wang Anshi, who once wrote him a poem praising him as "graceful as Xie Anshi, free-spirited as Tao Yuanming."

sentences.zh: 至是當國，更張法令，遼與之議論，浸浸咈意，日益見疏，於是坐與其長不相能，罷去。

translations.literal: Now when Anshi held power and reformed the laws, Liao debated with him, gradually clashing until he was daily more estranged. He was then dismissed for being incompatible with his superior.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi came to power and reformed the laws, Liao debated with him, gradually clashing until they grew daily more estranged. He was then dismissed for failing to get along with his superior.

sentences.zh: 久之，以太常寺奉禮郎監杭州軍資庫，轉運使使攝華亭縣。

translations.literal: Long after, as Ceremonial Officer of the Grand Music Supervisor he supervised the Hangzhou military provisions depot; the transport commissioner had him act as magistrate of Huating County.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he served as Ceremonial Officer of the Grand Music Supervisor supervising the Hangzhou military provisions depot, and the transport commissioner had him act as magistrate of Huating County.

sentences.zh: 他使者適有夙憾，思中以文法，因縣民忿爭相牽告，辭語連及，遂文致其罪。

translations.literal: Another transport envoy happened to hold an old grudge and sought to trap him by statute. Because county people in angry disputes mutual accused one another, words tangentially involved him, and they fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: Another transport envoy happened to hold an old grudge and sought to trap him through the law. When county people in angry disputes accused one another, their words tangentially implicated him, and charges were fabricated against him.

sentences.zh: 下獄引服，奪官流永州，遭父憂不得釋。

translations.literal: Thrown in prison he confessed; his office was stripped and he was exiled to Yongzhou. He met his father's death and could not be released.
translations.idiomatic: Thrown into prison he confessed; his office was stripped and he was exiled to Yongzhou. His father's death intervened and he could not be released.

sentences.zh: 更赦，始徙池州。

translations.literal: After a general amnesty he was only then transferred to Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty he was transferred to Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 留連江湖間累年，益偃蹇傲世。

translations.literal: Lingering among rivers and lakes for years, he grew increasingly defiant and proud toward the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lingering among rivers and lakes for years, he grew increasingly proud and defiant toward the world.

sentences.zh: 既至池，得九華、秋浦間，玩其林泉，喜曰：「使我自擇，不過爾耳。

translations.literal: Once at Chizhou he found the region between Jiuhua and Qiupu, enjoyed its forests and springs, and rejoiced: "Had I chosen for myself, it could be no more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Chizhou he found the country between Jiuhua and Qiupu, delighted in its forests and springs, and said joyfully, "Had I chosen for myself, it could be no more than this."

sentences.zh: 」既築室於齊山之上，名曰「雲巢」，好事者多往遊。

translations.literal: He built a house on Mount Qi named Cloud Nest, and many enthusiasts came to visit.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house on Mount Qi called Cloud Nest, and many enthusiasts came to visit.

sentences.zh: 遼追悔平生不自貴重，悉謝棄少習，杜門隱几，雖筆硯亦埃塵竟日。

translations.literal: Liao regretted that in life he had not treasured himself; he wholly abandoned his early habits, shut the door and leaned on a desk, and even brush and ink gathered dust all day.
translations.idiomatic: Liao regretted that in life he had not valued himself properly. He wholly abandoned his early habits, shut his door and leaned on his desk, and even brush and ink gathered dust all day.

sentences.zh: 間作為文章，雄奇峭麗，尤長於歌詩，曾鞏、蘇軾、黃庭堅皆與唱酬相往來，然竟不復起，元豐末，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: Occasionally composing essays—bold, strange, steep, and beautiful—he was especially skilled in songs and poetry. Zeng Gong, Su Shi, and Huang Tingjian all exchanged verses with him, yet he never returned to office. Late in the Yuanfeng era he died at fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally he composed essays that were bold, strange, steep, and beautiful, and he was especially skilled in songs and poetry. Zeng Gong, Su Shi, and Huang Tingjian all exchanged verses with him, yet he never returned to office. Late in the Yuanfeng era he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 從弟 括

translations.literal: Younger Cousin Kuo
translations.idiomatic: Younger Cousin Kuo

sentences.zh: 括，字存中，以父任為沭陽主簿。

translations.literal: Kuo, styled Cunzhong, through his father's appointment became chief clerk of Shuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo, courtesy name Cunzhong, through his father's appointment became chief clerk of Shuyang.

sentences.zh: 縣依沭水，乃職方氏所書「浸曰沂、沭」者，故跡漫為汙澤，括新其二坊，疏水為百渠九堰，以播節原委，得上田七十頃。

translations.literal: The county bordered the Shuyang River, where the Commandant's office recorded that floodwaters came from the Yi and Shu. Old traces had become stagnant marshes. Kuo rebuilt two embankments, dredged water into a hundred channels and nine weirs to distribute and regulate the source, and gained seventy qing of upper-grade fields.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered the Shuyang River, where the Commandant's office recorded that floodwaters came from the Yi and Shu. Old traces had become stagnant marshes. Kuo rebuilt two embankments and dredged the water into a hundred channels and nine weirs to distribute and regulate the flow, gaining seventy qing of upper-grade fields.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，編校昭文書籍，為館閣校勘，刪定三司條例。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, collated books at the Hall of Radiant Culture, served as library proofreader, and revised the Three Commissions regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, collated books at the Hall of Radiant Culture, served as library proofreader, and revised the Three Commissions regulations.

sentences.zh: 故事，三歲郊丘之制，有司按籍而行，藏其副，吏沿以干利。

translations.literal: By precedent, for the triennial suburban altar rites the departments proceeded by register, kept duplicates, and clerks exploited this for profit.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, for the triennial suburban altar rites the departments proceeded by register, kept duplicate records, and clerks exploited the practice for profit.

sentences.zh: 壇下張幔，距城數里為園囿，植采木、刻鳥獸綿絡其間。

translations.literal: Below the altar they stretched awnings; miles from the city they made garden grounds, planted ornamental trees, and carved birds and beasts densely interwoven among them.
translations.idiomatic: Below the altar they stretched awnings; miles from the city they laid out gardens, planted ornamental trees, and carved birds and beasts densely among them.

sentences.zh: 將事之夕，法駕臨觀，御端門、陳仗衛以閱嚴警，遊幸登賞，類非齋祠所宜。

translations.literal: On the eve of the rites the imperial carriage came to observe; at the Gate of Correctness they deployed guards to review security—excursions and awards quite unsuitable for a fasting sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rites the imperial carriage came to observe; at the Gate of Correctness guards were deployed to review security. Excursions and rewards of this sort were quite unsuitable for a fasting sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乘輿一器，而百工侍役者六七十輩。

translations.literal: One imperial vessel—and sixty or seventy artisans in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: For one imperial vessel, sixty or seventy artisans stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 括考禮沿革，為書曰《南郊式》。

translations.literal: Kuo researched ritual evolution and wrote a book called Southern Suburban Formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo researched the evolution of ritual and wrote a book called Southern Suburban Formulas.

sentences.zh: 即詔令點檢事務，執新式從事，所省萬計，神宗稱善。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict ordered inspection of affairs and execution according to the new formulas. Savings counted in the ten thousands, and Emperor Shenzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately ordered affairs inspected and carried out according to the new formulas. Savings ran into the tens of thousands, and Emperor Shenzong praised the result.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中允、檢正中書刑房、提舉司天監，日官皆市井庸販，法象圖器，大抵漫不知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Mentor, rectifier in the Secretariat Penal Section, and supervisor of the Astronomy Commission. The day officers were all marketplace peddlers, largely ignorant of instruments and charts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Mentor, rectifier in the Secretariat Penal Section, and supervisor of the Astronomy Commission. The day officers were all marketplace peddlers, largely ignorant of instruments and charts.

sentences.zh: 括始置渾儀、景表、五壺浮漏，招衛朴造新曆，募天下上太史占書，雜用士人，分方技科為五，後皆施用。

translations.literal: Kuo first installed an armillary sphere, gnomon table, and five-jar clepsydra; recruited Wei Pu to make a new calendar; solicited astrological texts from across the empire; mixed in scholars; and divided the technical disciplines into five categories—all later adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo first installed an armillary sphere, gnomon table, and five-jar clepsydra; recruited Wei Pu to make a new calendar; solicited astrological texts from across the empire; mixed in scholars; and divided the technical disciplines into five categories—all of which were later adopted.

sentences.zh: 加史館檢討。

translations.literal: He was added as historical compiler in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed historical compiler in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 淮南饑，遣括察訪，發常平錢粟，疏溝瀆，治廢田，以救水患。

translations.literal: During a Huainan famine he was sent to investigate; he released Ever-Normal Granary funds and grain, dredged channels, and reclaimed abandoned fields to relieve the flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: During a Huainan famine he was sent to investigate. He released Ever-Normal Granary funds and grain, dredged channels, and reclaimed abandoned fields to relieve the flood disaster.

sentences.zh: 遷集賢校理，察訪兩浙農田水利，遷太常丞、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, investigated farmland and waterworks in the Two Zhe circuits, and was promoted to Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler of the daily records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, investigated farmland and waterworks in the Two Zhe circuits, and was promoted to Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler of the daily records.

sentences.zh: 時大籍民車，人未諭縣官意，相挻為憂；

translations.literal: Then they greatly registered civilian carts, and people, not understanding the government's intent, spread anxiety among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the government greatly expanded registration of civilian carts, and people, not understanding its intent, spread anxiety among themselves.

sentences.zh: 又市易司患蜀鹽之不禁，欲盡實私井而輦解池鹽給之。

translations.literal: Also the Market Exchange Office worried that Sichuan salt was uncontrolled and wished to fully verify private wells and cart Jiechi salt to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The Market Exchange Office also worried that Sichuan salt was uncontrolled and wished to verify all private wells and transport Jiechi salt to supply them.

sentences.zh: 言者論二事如織，皆不省，括侍帝側，帝顧曰：「卿知籍車乎？

translations.literal: Memorialists argued both matters repeatedly, but no heed was taken. Kuo attended at the emperor's side, and the emperor turned and said: "Do you know about registering carts?
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued both matters at length, but no heed was taken. Kuo was attending at the emperor's side when the emperor turned and said, "Do you know about registering carts?"

sentences.zh: 」 曰：「知之。

translations.literal: He said: "I know."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I do."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What of it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What of it?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「敢問欲何用？

translations.literal: He replied: "May I ask what use is intended?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "May I ask what use is intended?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「北邊以馬取勝，非車不足以當之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The northern frontier wins with horses—not without carts can we match them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The northern frontier wins with horses; we cannot match them without carts."

sentences.zh: 」括曰：「車戰之利，見於歷世。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "The advantage of chariot warfare is seen through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said, "The advantage of chariot warfare is seen through the ages.

sentences.zh: 然古人所謂兵車者，輕車也，五御折旋，利於捷速。

translations.literal: Yet what the ancients called war chariots were light vehicles; the five driving skills in turning were advantageous for speed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the ancients called war chariots were light vehicles, and the five driving skills in turning were advantageous for speed.

sentences.zh: 今之民間輜車重大，日不能三十里，故世謂之太平車，但可施於無事之日爾。

translations.literal: Today's civilian supply carts are heavy and large—a day cannot cover thirty li; hence the age calls them Peace carts, fit only for untroubled days."
translations.idiomatic: Today's civilian supply carts are heavy and large and cannot cover thirty li in a day. Hence the age calls them Peace carts—fit only for untroubled days."

sentences.zh: 」帝喜曰：「人言無及此者，朕當思之。

translations.literal: The emperor, pleased, said: "No one has spoken to this point—I shall consider it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pleased, said, "No one has spoken to this point. I shall consider it."

sentences.zh: 」遂問蜀鹽事，對曰：「一切實私井而運解鹽，使一出於官售，誠善。

translations.literal: He then asked about Sichuan salt, and Kuo replied: "Fully verifying private wells and transporting Jiechi salt so that all sale comes from the government would truly be good.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked about Sichuan salt, and Kuo replied, "Fully verifying private wells and transporting Jiechi salt so that all sales come from the government would truly be good.

sentences.zh: 然忠萬、戎、瀘間夷界小井尤多，不可猝絕也，勢須列候加警，臣恐得不足償費。

translations.literal: Yet between Zhongwan, Rong, and Lu among the Yi border, small wells are especially numerous and cannot be suddenly cut off. Guards would have to be posted and alerts increased; I fear the gains would not repay the costs."
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the Yi borderlands of Zhongwan, Rong, and Lu, small wells are especially numerous and cannot be suddenly cut off. Guards would have to be posted and alerts increased, and I fear the gains would not repay the costs."

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 明日，二事俱寢。

translations.literal: The next day both matters were dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The next day both matters were dropped.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥，兼通進銀臺司，自中允至是才三月。

translations.literal: He was promoted to draft edict officer and concurrently Director of Palace Memorials—only three months from Junior Mentor to this.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to draft edict officer and concurrently Director of Palace Memorials—only three months from Junior Mentor to this.

sentences.zh: 為河北西路察訪使。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner inspecting the Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner inspecting the Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，銀冶，轉運司置官收其利，括言：「近寶則國貧，其勢必然；

translations.literal: Earlier, in silver smelting the transport office had set officials to collect profits. Kuo said: "Nearer treasure then the state grows poor—the tendency is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in silver smelting the transport office had set officials to collect profits. Kuo said, "The nearer treasure lies, the poorer the state becomes—the tendency is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 人眾則囊橐奸偽何以檢頤？

translations.literal: With more people, how can bags be inspected for fraud?
translations.idiomatic: With more people involved, how can bags be inspected for fraud?

sentences.zh: 朝廷歲遺契丹銀數十萬，以其非北方所有，故重而利之。

translations.literal: The court annually sends the Khitan hundreds of thousands in silver; because it is not native to the north, they value and profit from it.
translations.idiomatic: The court annually sends the Khitan hundreds of thousands in silver. Because it is not native to the north, they value and profit from it.

sentences.zh: 昔日銀城縣、銀坊城皆沒於彼，使其知鑿山之利，則中國之幣益輕，何賴歲餉，鄰釁將自茲始矣。」

translations.literal: Formerly Yincheng County and Yinfang Fort fell to them. If they know the profit of mining mountains, then China's currency will grow lighter still. How can we rely on annual tribute? Border conflict will begin from this."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yincheng County and Yinfang Fort fell to them. If they learn the profit of mining mountains, China's currency will grow lighter still. How can we rely on annual tribute? Border conflict will begin from this."

sentences.zh: 時賦近畿戶出馬備邊，民以為病，括言：「北地多馬而人習騎戰，猶中國之工強弩也。

translations.literal: Then households near the capital were levied to supply horses for border defense, and the people found it burdensome. Kuo said: "Northern lands have many horses and people skilled in mounted combat, like China's craft with strong crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: At the time households near the capital were levied to supply horses for border defense, and the people found it burdensome. Kuo said, "Northern lands have many horses and people skilled in mounted combat, just as China excels with strong crossbows.

sentences.zh: 今舍我之長技，強所不能，何以取勝。

translations.literal: Now abandoning our strengths and forcing what we cannot do—how can we win?
translations.idiomatic: Now we abandon our strengths and force what we cannot do—how can we win?"

sentences.zh: 」又邊人習兵，唯以挽強定最，而未必能貫革，謂宜以射遠入堅為法。

translations.literal: Also frontier troops train by drawing the bow hard for ranking, yet not necessarily piercing leather; he said they should take shooting far and penetrating hard as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that frontier troops trained by drawing the bow hard for ranking, yet not necessarily piercing leather, and that shooting far and penetrating hard should be made the standard.

sentences.zh: 如是者三十一事，詔皆可之。

translations.literal: Thirty-one such matters were all approved by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one such recommendations were all approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 遼蕭禧來理河東黃嵬地，留館不肯辭，曰：「必得請而後反。

translations.literal: The Khitan Xiao Xi came to negotiate Huangwei land in Hedong, stayed at the lodge refusing to leave, and said: "I must obtain approval before returning."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan Xiao Xi came to negotiate Huangwei land in Hedong, stayed at the lodge refusing to leave, and said, "I must obtain approval before returning."

sentences.zh: 」帝遣括往聘。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Kuo on embassy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Kuo on embassy.

sentences.zh: 括詣樞密院閱故牘，得頃歲所議疆地書，指古長城為境，今所爭蓋三十里遠，表論之。

translations.literal: Kuo went to the Bureau of Military Affairs, reviewed old files, and found boundary documents from recent years fixing the old Great Wall as the border. The present dispute was about thirty li. He memorialized on this.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo went to the Bureau of Military Affairs, reviewed old files, and found boundary documents from recent years fixing the old Great Wall as the border. The present dispute concerned about thirty li. He memorialized on this.

sentences.zh: 帝以休日開天章閣召對，喜曰：「大臣殊不究本末，幾誤國事。

translations.literal: On a rest day the emperor opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations for audience and, pleased, said: "Grand counsellors utterly failed to trace root and branch and nearly erred in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On a rest day the emperor opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations for audience and, pleased, said, "Grand counsellors utterly failed to trace matters to their root and branch and nearly erred in state affairs."

sentences.zh: 」命以畫圖示禧，禧議始屈。

translations.literal: He ordered maps shown to Xi, and Xi's argument began to bend.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered maps shown to Xi, and Xi's argument began to falter.

sentences.zh: 賜括白金千兩使行。

translations.literal: Kuo was bestowed one thousand taels of white silver for the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was bestowed one thousand taels of white silver for the mission.

sentences.zh: 至契丹庭，契丹相楊益戒來就議，括得地訟之籍數十，預使吏士誦之，益戒有所問，則顧吏舉以答。

translations.literal: At the Khitan court, Chancellor Yang Yijie came to negotiate. Kuo obtained dozens of land-dispute registers, had clerks memorize them beforehand, and when Yijie asked, he would look to a clerk who recited the answer.
translations.idiomatic: At the Khitan court, Chancellor Yang Yijie came to negotiate. Kuo obtained dozens of land-dispute registers and had clerks memorize them beforehand. When Yijie asked a question, Kuo would look to a clerk who recited the answer.

sentences.zh: 他日復問，亦如之。

translations.literal: Another day he asked again, and it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Yijie asked again, and it was the same.

sentences.zh: 益戒無以應，謾曰：「數里之地不忍，而輕絕好乎？

translations.literal: Yijie had no response and said frivolously: "A few li of land you cannot bear—yet you would lightly break good relations?
translations.idiomatic: Yijie had no response and said frivolously, "You cannot spare a few li of land, yet you would lightly break good relations?"

sentences.zh: 」括曰：「師直為壯，曲為老。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "An army righteous is vigorous; crooked is senile.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said, "An army righteous is vigorous; one crooked is senile.

sentences.zh: 今北朝棄先君之大信，以威用其民，非我朝之不利也。

translations.literal: Now the Northern Court abandons the great faith of former rulers and uses might on its people. This is not disadvantage to our court."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Northern Court abandons the great faith of former rulers and uses might on its people. That is not to our court's disadvantage."

sentences.zh: 」凡六會，契丹知不可奪，遂舍黃嵬而以天池請。

translations.literal: After six meetings the Khitan knew it could not be taken; they yielded Huangwei and requested Tianchi instead.
translations.idiomatic: After six meetings the Khitan knew the land could not be taken; they yielded Huangwei and requested Tianchi instead.

sentences.zh: 括乃還，在道圖其山川險易迂直，風俗之純龐，人情之向背，為《使契丹圖》，抄上之。

translations.literal: Kuo returned. On the road he mapped terrain difficulty, routes, customs pure and rough, and popular sentiment's alignment, made Map of Embassy to Khitan, and submitted a copy.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo returned. On the road he mapped the terrain's difficulties, routes, customs both pure and rough, and the people's inclinations, compiled Map of Embassy to Khitan, and submitted a copy.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士、權三司使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician and acting Fiscal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Academician and acting Fiscal Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗白事丞相府，吳充問曰：「自免役令下，民之詆訾者今未衰也，是果於民何如？

translations.literal: Once reporting at the chief counsellor's office, Wu Chong asked: "Since the exemption corvée edict, public criticism has not yet faded. Is it truly good for the people?
translations.idiomatic: Once, reporting at the chief counsellor's office, Wu Chong asked, "Since the exemption corvée edict, public criticism has not yet faded. Is it truly good for the people?"

sentences.zh: 」括曰：「以為不便者，特士大夫與邑居之人習於復除者爾，無足恤也。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "Those finding it inconvenient are merely scholar-officials and town dwellers accustomed to the old exemption system—not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said, "Those who find it inconvenient are merely scholar-officials and town dwellers accustomed to the old exemption system—not worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 獨微戶本無力役，而亦使出錢，則為可念。

translations.literal: Only petty households originally without corvée duty yet also required to pay money—that is lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Only petty households originally exempt from corvée duty yet also required to pay money—that is lamentable.

sentences.zh: 若悉弛之，使一無所預，則善矣。

translations.literal: If fully relaxed so they participate in nothing, that would be good."
translations.idiomatic: If they were fully exempted so as to participate in nothing, that would be good."

sentences.zh: 」充然其說，表行之。

translations.literal: Chong approved the view and memorialized to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong approved the view and memorialized to implement it.

sentences.zh: 蔡確論括首鼠乖剌，陰害司農法，以集賢院學士知宣州，明年，復龍圖閣待制、知審官院，又出知青州，未行，改延州。

translations.literal: Cai Que argued that Kuo was hedging and perverse and secretly harming the Revenue Commissioner law. He was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Xuanzhou. The next year he was restored as Hanlin Pending Academician and director of the Review Office, then sent out as prefect of Qingzhou. Before he departed he was reassigned to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que argued that Kuo was hedging and perverse and secretly undermining the Revenue Commissioner's law. He was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Xuanzhou. The next year he was restored as Hanlin Pending Academician and director of the Review Office, then sent out as prefect of Qingzhou. Before he departed he was reassigned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，悉以別賜錢為酒，命廛市良家子馳射角勝，有軼群之能者，自起酌酒以勞之，邊人歡激，執弓傅矢，唯恐不得進。

translations.literal: At his post he used all separately bestowed funds for wine, ordered sons of respectable families in the market to race, shoot, and compete, and those with outstanding ability he personally poured wine to reward. Border people were thrilled, grasped bows and fitted arrows, fearing only that they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he used all separately bestowed funds for wine and ordered sons of respectable families in the market to race, shoot, and compete. Those with outstanding ability he personally rewarded with wine. Border people were thrilled; they grasped bows and fitted arrows, fearing only that they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 越歲，得徹劄超乘者千餘，皆補中軍義從，威聲雄他府。

translations.literal: Within a year he obtained over a thousand superb mounted archers, all supplemented the central army volunteer followers, and his reputation towered over other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he obtained more than a thousand superb mounted archers, all of whom were enrolled as volunteer followers in the central army. His reputation towered over other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以副總管种諤西討援銀、宥功，加龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: For Vice Commander Zhong Nu's western campaign relieving Yin and You he was given merit and added as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: For Vice Commander Zhong Nu's western campaign relieving Yin and You he was given merit and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 朝廷出宿衛之師來戍，賞賚至再而不及鎮兵。

translations.literal: The court sent capital guard troops to garrison the frontier. Rewards were given twice but did not reach the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent capital guard troops to garrison the frontier. Rewards were distributed twice but did not reach the garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 括以為衛兵雖重，而無歲不戰者，鎮兵也。

translations.literal: Kuo held that though guard troops are weighty, those who fight every year are the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo held that though guard troops are esteemed, those who fight every year are the garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 今不均若是，且召亂。

translations.literal: Now such unequal distribution will summon disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Such unequal distribution would invite disorder.

sentences.zh: 乃藏敕書，而矯制賜緡錢數萬，以驛聞。

translations.literal: He hid the edict, forged an order granting tens of thousands in cash, and reported by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: He hid the edict, forged an order granting tens of thousands in cash, and reported by post relay.

sentences.zh: 詔報之曰：「此右府頒行之失，非卿察事機，必擾軍政。

translations.literal: The edict in response said: "This was the Military Affairs Bureau's distribution error. Had you not discerned circumstances, military order would surely have been disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict in response said, "This was the Military Affairs Bureau's distribution error. Had you not discerned the situation, military order would surely have been disturbed."

sentences.zh: 」自是，事不暇請者，皆得專之。

translations.literal: From then on, in matters not awaiting petition, he was permitted to decide independently.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, in matters not requiring prior approval, he was permitted to decide independently.

sentences.zh: 蕃漢將士自皇城使以降，許承制補授。

translations.literal: Tang and Han officers from Court Building commissioner down were permitted to appoint by provisional order.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Han officers from Court Building commissioner down were permitted to receive appointments by provisional order.

sentences.zh: 諤師次五原，值大雪，糧餉不繼，殿直劉歸仁率眾南奔，士卒二萬人皆潰入塞，居民怖駭。

translations.literal: Nu's army halted at Wuyuan. There was heavy snow and provisions did not continue. Palace Duty Officer Liu Guiren led the masses fleeing south, and twenty thousand soldiers all routed into the passes. Residents were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Nu's army halted at Wuyuan during heavy snow when provisions failed. Palace Duty Officer Liu Guiren led the troops fleeing south, and twenty thousand soldiers all routed into the passes. Residents were terrified.

sentences.zh: 括出東郊餞河東歸師，得奔者數千，問曰：「副都總管遣汝歸取糧，主者為何人？

translations.literal: Kuo went to the eastern suburbs to farewell Hedong returning troops, got thousands of fugitives, and asked: "The vice commander sent you back for grain—who is in charge?
translations.idiomatic: Kuo went to the eastern suburbs to see off Hedong troops returning and encountered thousands of fugitives. He asked, "The vice commander sent you back for grain—who is in charge?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「在後。

translations.literal: They said: "In the rear."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "In the rear."

sentences.zh: 」即諭令各歸屯。

translations.literal: He immediately instructed each to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately instructed each man to return to camp.

sentences.zh: 及暮，至者八百，未旬日，潰卒盡還。

translations.literal: By dusk eight hundred had arrived; within ten days all routed soldiers returned.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk eight hundred had arrived; within ten days all the routed soldiers returned.

sentences.zh: 括出按兵，歸仁至，括曰：「汝歸取糧，何以不持軍符？

translations.literal: Kuo went out inspecting troops. Guiren arrived, and Kuo said: "You returned for grain—why no military tally?
translations.idiomatic: Kuo went out to inspect the troops. When Guiren arrived, Kuo said, "You returned for grain—why did you carry no military tally?"

sentences.zh: 」歸仁不能對，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Guiren could not answer and was executed as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Guiren could not answer and was executed as an example.

sentences.zh: 經數日，帝使內侍劉惟簡來詰叛者，具以對。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor sent eunuch Liu Weijian to question the rebels, and Kuo fully reported.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the emperor sent eunuch Liu Weijian to question the rebels, and Kuo reported fully.

sentences.zh: 大將景思誼、曲珍拔夏人磨崖葭蘆浮圖城，括議築石堡以臨西夏，而給事中徐禧來，禧欲先城永樂。

translations.literal: Generals Jing Siyi and Qu Zhen took the Tangut towns Moyan, Jialu, and Fotu. Kuo proposed building Shibao to face Western Xia, but Chief Remonstrance Official Xu Xi came and wished first to fortify Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Jing Siyi and Qu Zhen captured the Tangut towns Moyan, Jialu, and Fotu. Kuo proposed building Shibao to face Western Xia, but Chief Remonstrance Official Xu Xi arrived and wished first to fortify Yongle.

sentences.zh: 詔禧護諸將往築，令括移府幷塞，以濟軍用。

translations.literal: An edict had Xi oversee the generals in building it and ordered Kuo to move his office to the frontier to supply military needs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Xi oversee the generals in building the fort and ordered Kuo to move his office to the frontier to supply military needs.

sentences.zh: 已而禧敗沒，括以夏人襲綏德，先往救之。

translations.literal: Before long Xi was defeated and killed. Because the Tanguts attacked Suide, Kuo went first to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xi was defeated and killed. When the Tanguts attacked Suide, Kuo went first to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 不能援永樂，坐謫均州團練副使。

translations.literal: Unable to relieve Yongle, he was demoted to militia vice commissioner of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to relieve Yongle, he was demoted to militia vice commissioner of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，徙秀州，繼以光祿少卿分司，居潤八年卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanyou era he was transferred to Xiuzhou, then given nominal posting as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets. He resided at Run eight years and died at sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was transferred to Xiuzhou, then given nominal posting as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets. He resided at Run eight years and died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 括博學善文，於天文、方志、律曆、音樂、醫藥、卜算，無所不通，皆有所論著。

translations.literal: Kuo was broadly learned and skilled in writing. In astronomy, geography, law and calendar, music, medicine, and divination he mastered all and had writings on each.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was broadly learned and skilled in writing. In astronomy, geography, law and calendar, music, medicine, and divination he mastered all and wrote on each.

sentences.zh: 又紀平日與賓客言者為《筆談》，多載朝廷故實、耆舊出處，傳於世。

translations.literal: He also recorded his daily talks with guests as Brush Talks, much on court lore and elders' careers, and it was passed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also recorded his daily conversations with guests as Brush Talks, which contains much on court lore and the careers of elders and was passed down in the world.

sentences.zh: 李大臨

translations.literal: Li Dalin
translations.idiomatic: Li Dalin

sentences.zh: 李大臨，字才元，成都華陽人。

translations.literal: Li Dalin, styled Caiyuan, was a man of Huayang in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dalin, courtesy name Caiyuan, was a native of Huayang in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為絳州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating officer of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating officer of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 杜衍安撫河東，薦為國子監直講、睦親宅講書。

translations.literal: Du Yan pacified Hedong and recommended him as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and tutor at the Mukqin Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan pacified Hedong and recommended him as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and tutor at the Mukqin Residence.

sentences.zh: 文彥博薦為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo recommended him as collator in the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo recommended him as collator in the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 考試舉人，誤收失聲韻者，責監滁州稅。

translations.literal: While examining candidates he mistakenly admitted one who failed the rhyme rules and was punished by supervising the Chuzhou tax.
translations.idiomatic: While examining candidates he mistakenly admitted one who failed the rhyme rules and was punished by being assigned to supervise the Chuzhou tax.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還故職。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗遣使賜館閣官御書，至大臨家，大臨貧無皂隸，方自秣馬，使者還奏，帝曰：「真廉士也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong once sent an envoy to bestow imperial writing on Hanlin officials. Arriving at Dalin's home, Dalin was poor and had no servants and was personally feeding his horse. The envoy reported back, and the emperor said: "A truly incorruptible man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong once sent an envoy to bestow imperial writing on Hanlin officials. Arriving at Dalin's home, he found Dalin poor and without servants, personally feeding his horse. The envoy reported back, and the emperor said, "A truly incorruptible man."

sentences.zh: 」以親老，請知廣安軍，徙邛州。

translations.literal: Because his parent was aged, he requested appointment as prefect of Guangan Jun and was transferred to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parent was aged, he requested appointment as prefect of Guangan Jun and was transferred to Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，為群牧判官、開封府推官。

translations.literal: On returning he served as livestock commissioner judge and Kaifeng investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he served as livestock commissioner judge and Kaifeng investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 神宗雅知其名，擢修起居注，進知制誥、糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong long knew his name, promoted him to compiler of the daily records, and advanced him to draft edict officer and supervisor of capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong had long known his name. He promoted him to compiler of the daily records and then to draft edict officer and supervisor of capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 言青苗法有害無益，王安石怒。

translations.literal: He spoke that the Green Sprouts law harmed without benefit, and Wang Anshi was angry.
translations.idiomatic: He stated that the Green Sprouts law harmed without benefit, and Wang Anshi was angry.

sentences.zh: 會李定除御史，宋敏求、蘇頌相繼封還詞命，次至大臨，大臨亦還之。

translations.literal: When Li Ding was appointed censor, Song Minqiu and Su Song successively sealed and returned the draft appointments. When it came to Dalin, Dalin also returned his.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ding was appointed censor, Song Minqiu and Su Song successively sealed and returned the draft appointments. When it came to Dalin, he also returned his.

sentences.zh: 帝批：「去歲詔書，臺官不拘官職奏舉，後未審更制也。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in the margin: "Last year's edict said Censorate officials were not bound by office for memorial recommendations. It is unclear whether the regulation was later changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in the margin, "Last year's edict said Censorate officials were not bound by office for memorial recommendations. It is unclear whether the regulation was later changed."

sentences.zh: 」頌、大臨合言：「故事，臺官必以員外郎、博士，近制但不限此，非謂選人亦許之也。

translations.literal: Song and Dalin jointly stated: "By precedent, Censorate officials had to be outside-office appointees or Masters of Philosophy. The recent regulation merely did not limit this—it did not mean common selectees were also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Dalin jointly stated, "By precedent, Censorate officials had to be outside-office appointees or Masters of Philosophy. The recent regulation merely did not limit this—it did not mean common selectees were also permitted.

sentences.zh: 定以初等職官超朝籍，躐憲臺，國朝未有。

translations.literal: Ding, as an entry-level official, leapfrogged the court registry and skipped onto the Censorate—never in our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, as an entry-level official, leapfrogged the court registry and skipped onto the Censorate—something never before seen in our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 幸門一開，名器有限，安得人人滿其意哉。

translations.literal: Once favor's gate opens, famous posts are limited. How can everyone have his wish fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: Once the gate of favor opens, prestigious posts are limited. How can everyone have his wish fulfilled?"

sentences.zh: 」復詔諭數四，頌、大臨故爭不已，乃以累格詔命，皆歸班，大臨以工部郎中出知汝州。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts instructed them four times, but Song and Dalin still argued unceasingly. Then for repeatedly blocking edicts both returned to the ranks. Dalin went out as prefect of Ruzhou as Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts instructed them four times, but Song and Dalin still argued unceasingly. Then for repeatedly blocking edicts both returned to the ranks. Dalin went out as prefect of Ruzhou in the capacity of Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 辰溪貢丹砂，道葉縣，其二篋化為雙雉，鬥山谷間。

translations.literal: Chenxi tribute cinnabar passed through Ye County; two boxes turned into paired pheasants fighting in a mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxi tribute cinnabar passed through Ye County when two boxes turned into paired pheasants fighting in a mountain valley.

sentences.zh: 耕者獲之，人疑為盜，械送於府。

translations.literal: Farmers caught them; people suspected thieves and shackled and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers caught them; people suspected they were thieves and had them shackled and sent to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大臨識其異，訊得實，釋耕者。

translations.literal: Dalin recognized the strangeness, interrogated and got the truth, and released the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin recognized the strangeness of the affair, interrogated and learned the truth, and released the farmers.

sentences.zh: 徙知梓州，加集賢殿修撰，復天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He was transferred as prefect of Zizhou, added as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Worthies, and restored as Hanlin Pending Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as prefect of Zizhou, added as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Worthies, and restored as Hanlin Pending Academician.

sentences.zh: 甫七十，致仕七年而卒。

translations.literal: Just seventy, he retired; seven years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: At just seventy he retired; seven years later he died.

sentences.zh: 大臨清整有守，論議識大體，因爭李定後名益重，世並宋敏求、蘇頌稱為「熙寧三舍人」云。

translations.literal: Dalin was pure, orderly, and principled; his discourse grasped the larger whole. After contending over Li Ding his fame grew heavier, and the world jointly with Song Minqiu and Su Song called them the Three Hanlin Draft Officers of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin was pure, orderly, and principled, and his discourse grasped the larger whole. After contending over Li Ding his fame grew still greater, and the world jointly with Song Minqiu and Su Song called them the Three Hanlin Draft Officers of Xining.

sentences.zh: 呂夏卿

translations.literal: Lu Xiaqing
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaqing

sentences.zh: 呂夏卿，字縉叔，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiaqing, styled Jinshu, was a man of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaqing, courtesy name Jinshu, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為江寧尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Jiangning district captain.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Jiangning district captain.

sentences.zh: 編修《唐書》成，直秘閣、同知禮院。

translations.literal: When the compilation of the New Tang History was completed, he became Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and Associate Director of the Rites Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation of the New Tang History was completed, he became Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and Associate Director of the Rites Court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗選任大臣，求治道，夏卿陳時務五事，且言：「天下之勢，不能常安，當於未然之前救其弊；

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong selected and appointed grand counsellors and sought the way of governance. Xiaqing presented five matters of the times and said: "The empire's condition cannot always be safe; one should remedy its ills before they arise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong selected and appointed grand counsellors and sought the way of governance. Xiaqing presented five matters of the times and said, "The empire's condition cannot always be safe; one should remedy its ills before they arise.

sentences.zh: 事至而圖之，恐無及已。

translations.literal: When matters arrive and one then plans, I fear it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: When matters arrive and one then plans, I fear it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷頗采其策。

translations.literal: The court largely adopted his policies.
translations.idiomatic: The court largely adopted his policies.

sentences.zh: 英宗世，歷史館檢討、同修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: In Yingzong's reign he served as historical compiler, compiler of the daily records, and draft edict officer.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingzong's reign he served as historical compiler, compiler of the daily records, and draft edict officer.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗訪以政，對曰：「兩朝不惜金帛以和二邊，脫民鋒鏑之禍，古未有也。

translations.literal: The emperor once consulted him on governance, and he replied: "Two reigns did not spare gold and silk to reconcile the two frontiers and freed the people from spear and arrow calamity—unprecedented in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once consulted him on governance, and he replied, "Two reigns did not spare gold and silk to reconcile the two frontiers and freed the people from the calamity of spear and arrow—unprecedented in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 願勿失前好。

translations.literal: I wish not to lose former goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that former goodwill not be lost."

sentences.zh: 」出知潁州，得奇疾，身體日縮，卒時才如小兒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Yingzhou, he contracted a strange illness; his body daily shrank, and at death he was only the size of a child. He was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Yingzhou, he contracted a strange illness. His body shrank daily, and at death he was only the size of a child. He was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 夏卿學長於史，貫穿唐事，博采傳記雜說數百家，折衷整比。

translations.literal: Xiaqing's learning excelled in history. He penetrated Tang affairs, broadly gathered hundreds of biographies and miscellanies, and weighed and arranged them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing's learning excelled in history. He penetrated Tang affairs, broadly gathered hundreds of biographies and miscellanies, and weighed and arranged them.

sentences.zh: 又通譜學，創為世係諸表，於《新唐書》最有功云。

translations.literal: He also mastered genealogy, created lineage tables, and was most meritorious on the New Tang History.
translations.idiomatic: He also mastered genealogy, created lineage tables, and contributed most to the New Tang History.

sentences.zh: 祖無擇

translations.literal: Zu Wuzhai
translations.idiomatic: Zu Wuzhai

sentences.zh: 祖無擇，字擇之，上蔡人。

translations.literal: Zu Wuzhai, styled Zhezhi, was a man of Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Wuzhai, courtesy name Zhezhi, was a native of Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 進士高第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination with top rank.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination with top rank.

sentences.zh: 歷知南康軍、海州，提點淮南廣東刑獄、廣南轉運使，入直集賢院。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Nankang Jun and Haizhou, judicial intendant for Huainan and Guangdong, transport commissioner for Guangnan, and entered the Hanlin in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as prefect of Nankang Jun and Haizhou, judicial intendant for Huainan and Guangdong, transport commissioner for Guangnan, and entered the Hanlin in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時封孔子後為文宣公，無擇言：「前代所封曰宗聖，曰奉聖，曰崇聖，曰恭聖，曰褒聖；

translations.literal: When Confucius's descendant was enfeoffed as Duke of Literary Propagation, Wuzhai said: "Former dynasties enfeoffed him as Duke of Ancestral Sage, Duke of Serving Sage, Duke of Honored Sage, Duke of Reverent Sage, and Duke of Commended Sage.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius's descendant was enfeoffed as Duke of Literary Propagation, Wuzhai said, "Former dynasties enfeoffed him as Duke of Ancestral Sage, Duke of Serving Sage, Duke of Honored Sage, Duke of Reverent Sage, and Duke of Commended Sage.

sentences.zh: 唐開元中，尊孔子為文宣王，遂以祖諡而加後嗣，非禮也。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era of Tang, Confucius was honored as King of Literary Propagation, and then his ancestral posthumous title was applied to the descendant—not ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era of Tang, Confucius was honored as King of Literary Propagation, and then his ancestral posthumous title was applied to the descendant—not ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」於是下近臣議，改為衍聖公。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was submitted to near ministers for deliberation, and the title was changed to Duke of Propagating Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the matter was submitted to near ministers for deliberation, and the title was changed to Duke of Propagating Sage.

sentences.zh: 出知袁州。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自慶曆詔天下立學，十年間其敝徒文具，無命教之實。

translations.literal: Since the Qingli edict ordering schools established throughout the empire, for ten years its defects amounted to mere paper formalities, with no reality of mandated instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Qingli edict had ordered schools established across the empire, a decade had passed in which the system had degenerated into empty paperwork, with no genuine instruction being provided.

sentences.zh: 無擇首建學官，置生徒，郡國弦誦之風。

translations.literal: Wuzai was the first to establish school officials and enroll students, and the sound of chanting lessons in the prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzai was the first to establish school officials and enroll students, and from this the culture of chanting lessons in the prefectures and commanderies began.

sentences.zh: 由此始盛。

translations.literal: From this it first flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From that point it began to flourish.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注、知制誥，加龍圖閣直學士、權知開封府，進學士，知鄭、杭二州。

translations.literal: He co-compiled the Veritable Records and drafted imperial edicts; was promoted to Hanlin associate academician of the Longtu Hall, acting prefect of Kaifeng, advanced to academician, and served as prefect of Zheng and Hang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He co-compiled the Veritable Records and served as drafter of imperial edicts; he was promoted to Hanlin associate academician of the Longtu Hall and acting prefect of Kaifeng, advanced to full academician, and served as prefect of Zheng and Hang.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was put in charge of the Tongjin Yintai Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, Wuzai was placed in charge of the Office for Memorials to the Throne.

sentences.zh: 初，詞臣作誥命，許受潤筆物。

translations.literal: At first, when drafting officers composed patent letters of appointment, they were permitted to accept brush-wetting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In those days, when literary officials drafted patent letters of appointment, they were allowed to accept gratuities.

sentences.zh: 王安石與無擇同知制誥，安石辭一家所饋不獲，義不欲取，置諸院梁上，安石憂去，無擇用為公費，安石聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi and Wuzai served together as edict drafters. Anshi tried to refuse a gift from one family but could not; deeming it improper to accept, he placed it on a beam in the office courtyard. When Anshi left on account of the matter, Wuzai applied the gift to office expenses. Anshi heard of this and detested him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi and Wuzai served together as edict drafters. Anshi tried to refuse a gift from one family but could not; considering it improper to accept, he placed it on a beam in the office courtyard. When Anshi departed over the affair, Wuzai applied the gift to office expenses. Anshi heard of this and came to detest him.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，安石得政，乃諷監司求無擇罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining period, once Anshi had gained power, he prompted circuit intendants to seek Wuzai's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xining period, after Anshi had seized power, he prompted circuit commissioners to find grounds to charge Wuzai.

sentences.zh: 知明州苗振以貪聞，御史王子韶使兩浙，廉其狀，事連無擇。

translations.literal: Miao Zhen, prefect of Ming Prefecture, was known for greed; the censor Wang Zishao toured the two Zhe circuits, investigated his conduct, and the affair implicated Wuzai.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Zhen, prefect of Ming, had a reputation for corruption. The censor Wang Zishao was sent to the two Zhe circuits to investigate, and the case implicated Wuzai as well.

sentences.zh: 子韶，小人也，請遣內侍自京師逮赴秀州獄。

translations.literal: Zishao, a petty man, requested that an inner-court attendant be sent from the capital to arrest Wuzai and bring him to the jail at Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zishao, a base man, asked that an inner-court eunuch be sent from the capital to arrest Wuzai and bring him to the jail at Xiu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌言無擇列侍從，不當與故吏對曲直，御史張戩亦救之，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Su Song said Wuzai ranked among the imperial attendants and should not be matched in right and wrong against former subordinates; the censor Zhang Kan also came to his rescue—all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song argued that Wuzai, as a member of the imperial entourage, should not be tried in a petty dispute against a former subordinate; the censor Zhang Kan also intervened on his behalf—but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及獄成，無貪狀，但得其貸官錢、接部民坐及乘船過制而已。

translations.literal: When the case concluded, there was no evidence of greed, but only that he had lent official funds, borne responsibility for a subordinate's offense, and exceeded boat regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the investigation concluded, no corruption was found—only that he had lent out official funds, been implicated in a subordinate's offense, and exceeded regulations governing his official boat.

sentences.zh: 遂謫忠正軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He was demoted to military commissioner deputy of the Zhongzheng Army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to military commissioner deputy of the Zhongzheng Army circuit.

sentences.zh: 安石猶為帝言：「陛下遣一御史出，即得無擇罪，及知朝廷於事但不為，未有為之而無效者。

translations.literal: Anshi still said to the emperor: "Your Majesty sent out one censor and immediately obtained Wuzai's crimes, thus knowing that in affairs the court merely does not act—there is never action without effect.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi still told the emperor, "Your Majesty dispatched a single censor and at once uncovered Wuzai's offenses. This shows that when the court fails in its affairs, it is simply because it chooses not to act—never because action yields no result."

sentences.zh: 」尋復光祿卿、秘書監、集賢院學士，主管西京御史臺，移知信陽軍，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to the posts of Director of the Imperial Household, Supervisor of the Imperial Library, and Hanlin academician of the Jixian Hall, placed in charge of the Censorate at the Western Capital, transferred to command Xinyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to the posts of Director of the Imperial Household, Supervisor of the Imperial Library, and Hanlin academician of the Jixian Hall, and placed in charge of the Censorate at the Western Capital; he was later transferred to command Xinyang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 無擇為人好義，篤於師友，少從孫明復學經術，又從穆修為文章。

translations.literal: Wuzai was by nature fond of righteousness and devoted to teachers and friends. In youth he studied the classics under Sun Mingfu and later studied literary composition under Mu Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzai was a man of righteous character and deep loyalty to teachers and friends. In youth he studied the classics under Sun Mingfu and later studied literary composition under Mu Xiu.

sentences.zh: 兩人死，力求其遺文彙次之，傳於世。

translations.literal: When both men died, he strove to collect their surviving writings and compile them, transmitting them to the world.
translations.idiomatic: After both men died, he worked hard to gather their surviving writings, compile them, and pass them on to posterity.

sentences.zh: 以言語政事為時名卿，用小累鍛煉放棄，訖不復振，士論惜之。

translations.literal: Renowned among his age as a minister distinguished in speech and administration, he was forged and cast aside over a minor offense and never restored, and opinion among scholars lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned in his day as a leading minister of speech and statecraft, he was broken on a minor charge and cast aside, never to rise again—a loss deeply regretted among the literati.

sentences.zh: 論曰：沈遘以文學致身，而長於治才。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Shen Gou rose through literary learning and excelled in administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Shen Gou rose through literary learning and excelled in administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 沈括博物洽聞，貫乎幽深，措諸政事，又極開敏。

translations.literal: Shen Kuo was broadly learned and well informed, penetrating the deepest matters; when applied to government affairs, he was also extremely quick and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kuo was broadly learned and penetratingly informed, reaching into the deepest matters; when he turned to government affairs, he proved equally quick and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 呂夏卿號稱史才，尤精譜諜之學。

translations.literal: Lu Xiaqing was acclaimed as a historian and was especially skilled in genealogical studies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaqing was acclaimed as a historian and was especially skilled in genealogical studies.

sentences.zh: 宋之縉紳，士各精其能，學不苟且，故能然也。

translations.literal: Among the gentry of Song, each man refined his own capacity; learning was never perfunctory—thus they could be so.
translations.idiomatic: Among the gentry of the Song, each man mastered his own specialty; learning was never perfunctory—and that is why they achieved what they did.

sentences.zh: 李大臨官居繳駁，克舉其職；

translations.literal: Li Dalin, holding office in memorial review, fully performed his duties;
translations.idiomatic: Li Dalin, in his post reviewing memorials, fully performed his duties;

sentences.zh: 祖無擇治郡所至，能修校官，是皆班班可紀者。

translations.literal: wherever Wuzai governed prefectures, he was able to restore and maintain schools—each of these is clearly worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: wherever Wuzai governed, he was able to restore and maintain schools—each of these is clearly worth recording.

sentences.zh: 然大臨以論李定絀，無擇以忤安石廢棄終身，即是亦足以知二人之賢矣。

translations.literal: Yet Dalin was demoted for criticizing Li Ding, and Wuzai was cast aside for life for opposing Anshi—this alone suffices to show the worth of both men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dalin was demoted for criticizing Li Ding, and Wuzai was cast aside for life for opposing Anshi—this alone suffices to show the worth of both men.

sentences.zh: 程師孟

translations.literal: Cheng Shimeng
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shimeng

sentences.zh: 程師孟，字公闢，吳人。

translations.literal: Cheng Shimeng, courtesy name Gongbi, was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shimeng, courtesy name Gongbi, was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科。

translations.literal: He passed the presented scholars examination in the first rank of the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 累知南康軍、楚州，提點夔路刑獄。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Nankang Army and Chuzhou, and as judicial intendant for the Kuizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as prefect of Nankang and Chuzhou, and as judicial intendant for the Kuizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 瀘戎數犯渝州，邊使者治所在萬州，相去遠，有警率浹日乃至，師孟奏徙於渝。

translations.literal: The Lu barbarians repeatedly raided Yuzhou; border envoys had their seats at Wanzhou, far away; when alarms arose they generally took a full day to arrive. Shimeng memorialized to move the seat to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu tribes repeatedly raided Yuzhou. Border commissioners were stationed at Wanzhou, far away, so that when alarms arose it generally took a full day for them to respond. Shimeng memorialized to move the seat to Yu.

sentences.zh: 夔部無常平粟，建請置倉，適凶歲，振民不足，即矯發他儲，不俟報。

translations.literal: The Kuizhou region had no Ever-Normal Granary grain; he memorialized to establish a storehouse. In a year of famine, the relief for the people was insufficient, so he falsely issued other reserves without awaiting approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuizhou region had no Ever-Normal Granary grain, so he memorialized to establish a storehouse. When famine struck, relief for the people proved insufficient, and he requisitioned other reserves on his own authority without awaiting approval.

sentences.zh: 吏懼，白不可。

translations.literal: The clerks feared this and reported that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks were alarmed and reported that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 師孟曰：「必俟報，餓者盡死矣。

translations.literal: Shimeng said: "If we must await approval, the starving will all be dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng said, "If we must await approval, the starving will all be dead."

sentences.zh: 」竟發之。

translations.literal: " In the end he released the grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he released the grain.

sentences.zh: 徙河東路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 晉地多土山，旁接川谷，春夏大雨，水濁如黃河，俗謂之「天河」，可溉灌。

translations.literal: The Jin region had many earthen hills adjoining valleys; in spring and summer, when heavy rains fell, the water was muddy like the Yellow River—the people called it the "Heaven River," and it could be used for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin region had many earthen hills adjoining valleys; in spring and summer, when heavy rains fell, the water ran muddy like the Yellow River. The people called it the "Heaven River," and it could be used for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 師孟出錢開渠築堰，淤良田萬八千頃，裒其事為《水利圖經》，頒之州縣。

translations.literal: Shimeng spent his own funds to open channels and build dikes, reclaiming eighteen thousand mu of fertile fields; he compiled the project into the Waterworks Gazetteer and distributed it to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng spent his own funds to open channels and build dikes, reclaiming eighteen thousand mu of fertile fields; he compiled an account of the work into the Waterworks Gazetteer and distributed it to prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 為度支判官，知洪州，積石為江隄，浚章溝，揭北牐以節水升降，後無水患。

translations.literal: As vice-director of the Revenue Bureau, he served as prefect of Hongzhou, piled stones to form a river dike, dredged the Zhang Canal, and raised the northern sluice gate to regulate the rise and fall of water; afterward there were no further flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-director of the Revenue Bureau, he served as prefect of Hongzhou, piled stones to form a river dike, dredged the Zhang Canal, and raised the northern sluice gate to regulate the rise and fall of water; afterward there were no further flood disasters.

sentences.zh: 判三司都磨勘司。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Three Departments General Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Three Departments General Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 接伴契丹使，蕭惟輔曰：「白溝之地當兩屬，今南朝植柳數里，而以北人漁界河為罪，豈理也哉？

translations.literal: While receiving the Khitan envoy, Xiao Weifu said: "The land at the Bai Trench ought to belong to both sides equally. Now the Southern Court has planted willows for several li, yet condemns northerners for fishing in the border river—is this reasonable?
translations.idiomatic: While receiving the Khitan envoy, Xiao Weifu said, "The land at the Bai Trench ought to belong to both sides equally. Now the Southern Court has planted willows for several li, yet condemns northerners for fishing in the border river—is this reasonable?"

sentences.zh: 」師孟曰：「兩朝當守誓約，涿郡有案牘可覆視，君舍文書，滕口說，遽欲生事耶？

translations.literal: Shimeng said: "Both courts should uphold their sworn covenant. At Zhuo Prefecture there are records that can be reviewed. You abandon the documents and speak empty words—do you suddenly wish to stir up trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng replied, "Both courts should uphold their sworn covenant. At Zhuo Prefecture there are records that can be reviewed. You abandon the documents and speak empty words—do you suddenly wish to stir up trouble?"

sentences.zh: 」惟輔愧謝。

translations.literal: " Weifu, ashamed, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Weifu, ashamed, apologized.

sentences.zh: 出為江西轉運使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as transport commissioner for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner for Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 盜發袁州，州吏為耳目，久不獲。

translations.literal: A robbery occurred in Yuan Prefecture; prefectural clerks served as informants, and for a long time the culprits were not captured.
translations.idiomatic: A robbery occurred in Yuan Prefecture; prefectural clerks served as informants, and for a long time the culprits were not captured.

sentences.zh: 師孟械吏數輩送獄，盜即成擒。

translations.literal: Shimeng shackled several clerks and sent them to jail; the robbers were immediately seized.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng shackled several clerks and sent them to jail; the robbers were immediately seized.

sentences.zh: 加直昭文館、知福州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to direct access to the Zhaowen Hall and served as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct access to the Zhaowen Hall and served as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 築子城，建學舍，治行最東南。

translations.literal: He built an inner wall, constructed school buildings, and his administration ranked highest in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: He built an inner wall, constructed school buildings, and his administration ranked highest in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州，州城為儂寇所毀，他日有警，民駭竄，方伯相踵至，皆言土疏惡不可築。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangzhou. The prefectural walls had been destroyed by the Nong rebels; when alarms arose later, the people fled in panic. Regional governors arrived one after another, all saying the soil was loose and poor and that walls could not be built.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangzhou. The prefectural walls had been destroyed by the Nong rebels; when alarms arose later, the people fled in panic. Regional governors arrived one after another, all saying the soil was loose and poor and that walls could not be built.

sentences.zh: 師孟在廣六年，作西城。

translations.literal: Shimeng was at Guang for six years and built the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng spent six years at Guang and built the western wall.

sentences.zh: 及交阯陷邕管，聞廣守備固，不敢東。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi fell upon Yong and Guan, it heard that Guang's defenses were solid and did not dare advance eastward.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi fell upon Yong and Guan, it heard that Guang's defenses were solid and did not dare advance eastward.

sentences.zh: 時師孟已召還，朝廷念前功，以為給事中、集賢殿修撰、判都水監。

translations.literal: By then Shimeng had already been recalled; the court, mindful of his earlier achievements, appointed him supervising censor, Hanlin compiler of the Jixian Hall, and director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shimeng had already been recalled; the court, mindful of his earlier achievements, appointed him supervising censor, Hanlin compiler of the Jixian Hall, and director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 賀契丹生辰，至涿州，契丹命席，迎者正南向，涿州官西向，宋使介東向。

translations.literal: While congratulating the Khitan emperor on his birthday, he reached Zhuo Prefecture; the Khitan arranged the seating—the greeters faced due south, the Zhuo officials faced west, and the Song envoys and attendants faced east.
translations.idiomatic: While congratulating the Khitan emperor on his birthday, he reached Zhuo Prefecture; the Khitan arranged the seating—the greeters faced due south, the Zhuo officials faced west, and the Song envoys and attendants faced east.

sentences.zh: 師孟曰：「是卑我也。

translations.literal: Shimeng said: "This demeans me.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng said, "This demeans me."

sentences.zh: 」不就列。

translations.literal: " He would not take his place.
translations.idiomatic: He would not take his place.

sentences.zh: 自日昃爭至暮，從者失色，師孟辭氣益厲，叱儐者易之，於是更與迎者東西向。

translations.literal: From mid-afternoon they argued until evening; his attendants turned pale, but Shimeng's words and bearing grew fiercer. He rebuked the ushers to change the arrangement, and greeters and guests were then seated facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-afternoon they argued until evening; his attendants turned pale, but Shimeng's words and bearing grew fiercer. He rebuked the ushers to change the arrangement, and greeters and guests were then seated facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 明日，涿人餞於郊，疾馳過不顧；

translations.literal: The next day the people of Zhuo saw him off in the suburbs; he galloped past without looking back;
translations.idiomatic: The next day the people of Zhuo saw him off in the suburbs; he galloped past without looking back;

sentences.zh: 涿人移雄州，以為言，坐罷歸班。

translations.literal: the Zhuo people reported this at Xiong Prefecture, and he was dismissed and returned to the regular roster.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhuo people reported this at Xiong Prefecture, and he was dismissed and returned to the regular roster.

sentences.zh: 復起知越州、青州，遂致仕，以光祿大夫卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He was later reappointed prefect of Yue and Qing, then retired, and died as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed prefect of Yue and Qing, then retired, and died as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness at age seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 師孟累領劇鎮，為政簡而嚴，罪非死者不以屬吏。

translations.literal: Shimeng repeatedly held difficult prefectures; his government was simple yet strict, and for offenses short of death he did not hand cases to subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng repeatedly held difficult prefectures; his government was simple yet strict, and for offenses short of death he did not hand cases to subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 發隱擿伏如神，得豪惡不逞跌宕者，必痛懲艾之，至剿絕乃已，所部肅然。

translations.literal: In exposing hidden wrongs he was like a spirit; when he caught powerful evildoers who would not submit, he always punished them severely until they were utterly destroyed, and the regions under his rule were brought to order.
